sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which two documents must you carry and what three cabin checks come before driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Before driving, carry a valid Learner's Permit or driver's license and the vehicle registration card, adjust your seat and mirrors, and make sure you and every passenger wear a seat belt.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What fundamental rule governs vehicle control every moment you are behind the wheel, and why?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: A basic driving rule is that the driver must control the vehicle at all times to avoid a crash, because the driver is responsible for operating it safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Where does a defensive driver keep looking, and what two adjustments does early scanning prepare for?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Defensive driving means constantly watching the front, sides and rear of your vehicle and searching ahead so you are ready to change speed or lanes and have time to spot risks.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What six habits help manage roadway risk, including what you must never assume about other motorists?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: To manage risk, adjust speed, position and direction to the road, keep control, give yourself more reaction time, signal your plans, keep a safe gap, and never assume other drivers will do what they should.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What does yielding the right-of-way mean in practice, and what mindset trap must you avoid?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Yielding the right-of-way means letting another vehicle, bicyclist or pedestrian go first, and you should never assume you automatically have the right to go first.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Who yields when one vehicle reaches an intersection later versus when two vehicles arrive together?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.memory_hook: First arrives goes; ties yield right
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Yield to the driver who reaches an intersection before you, and when two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: At a four-way stop, which tie-breaker applies and which three road users inside the intersection get priority?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: At a four-way intersection with stop signs, yield to the driver on your right, and always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still in the intersection.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Whom must you yield to when stopped on the stem of a T intersection or facing a yield sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: When you stop at a T intersection, yield to drivers already on the through road, and when a yield sign faces you, yield to other drivers.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: When making a left turn, which stream of traffic holds priority over your turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: When turning left, yield to drivers in the opposing lane, meaning traffic coming from the opposite direction.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Who holds the right-of-way when you pull out of a driveway or merge off a highway acceleration ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Yield to drivers on the road when you enter it from a driveway or private road, and to drivers already on the highway when you are on an entrance or acceleration ramp.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: When does the yield-to-the-right rule decide intersection order versus first-to-arrive?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: First to arrive goes first at an intersection, and only when two drivers arrive together does the driver on the right get the right-of-way.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Contrast which traffic stream you yield to during a left turn versus pulling from a driveway or ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic, while a driver entering from a driveway, private road or acceleration ramp yields to traffic already on the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What conditions does a posted speed sign assume, and whose job is choosing a safe pace?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: The posted speed limit is the highest legal speed under ideal conditions, and you remain responsible for driving at a safe speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Up to the posted limit, what speed is safest in normal flow, and why is creeping much slower risky?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The safest speed is the pace most traffic is moving, up to the limit, because driving slower than others makes them pass you constantly and raises crash risk.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What five control, perception, and impact problems make speeding one of the top crash causes?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.memory_hook: Weaker control, longer stops, harder hits
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Speeding is one of the most common crash causes: it weakens your handling of curves and obstacles, lengthens stopping, slows hazard recognition, misleads others judging your distance, and increases crash force.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Under Maryland Vehicle Law, when may you drive below a posted speed limit, and may you ever drive above it?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Maryland Vehicle Law requires a reasonable speed with awareness of hazards; you may drive below the posted limit for conditions, but driving above it is illegal.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: For what kinds of road geometry, slick surfaces, busy zones, structures, or crossings does Maryland advise slowing?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Slow down for sharp curves or hills, slippery roads, places with pedestrians or animals, shopping centers, parking lots and downtowns, heavy traffic, narrow bridges and tunnels, toll plazas, schools, playgrounds, residential streets and railroad grade crossings.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Compare the legality of slowing below the limit in bad conditions versus speeding to match fast traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Driving below the posted limit for bad conditions is legal, but exceeding the posted limit is illegal even if traffic around you is faster.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: How do train tracks meet the roadway at a railroad grade crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: A railroad grade crossing is a place where the tracks are level with the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Which four human, surface, and mechanical factors control how far your car travels while stopping?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Stopping distance depends on how long it takes you to notice danger, the type and condition of the road, your tire tread and your brakes.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Where should you choose to park, and how should your tires sit relative to traffic and any curb?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Park only where parking is clearly intended, as far from traffic as possible, and as close to the curb as possible when there is one.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: What four steps secure your vehicle and protect passing traffic before you walk away from a parked car?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: After parking, set the parking brake, put a manual car in gear or an automatic in park, check mirrors and traffic before opening the door, and take your keys.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What causes most rear-end collisions, and how many seconds of following space does the MVA advise?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Following too closely causes most rear-end crashes, and the MVA recommends at least three to four seconds of following distance in ideal conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How do you use a roadside landmark and counting phrase to verify at least a three-second gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: To check your gap, pick a fixed reference point such as a bridge, overpass, sign or mile marker and count from when the car ahead passes it; reaching three one thousand before you get there means you are at least three seconds back.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: To how many seconds should you widen your following gap behind transit buses or delivery vans?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Behind vehicles that stop often, such as buses and delivery vans, increase your following distance to four or five seconds, or more if needed.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does Maryland's standard dry-road following gap step up when trailing frequent-stopping buses or vans?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: The ideal-condition minimum gap is three to four seconds, which grows to four or five seconds or more behind buses and delivery vans that stop often.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Contrast how following distance is measured against the four factors that determine stopping distance?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.memory_hook: Seconds count gap; four factors stop
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Following distance is measured in seconds against a fixed reference point, whereas stopping distance depends on reaction time, road surface, tire tread and brakes.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: How should you hold your lane, and where is changing lanes specifically off-limits?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Drive within a single lane, change lanes only when it is safe, and do not drift over lane lines or change lanes inside an intersection.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Which three situations allow driving left of the roadway center in Maryland?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Keep right of the center of the road unless you are passing a vehicle going your way, a sign or signal permits it, or an obstruction makes moving over necessary.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: What five habits prepare you cleanly before executing any street turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.memory_hook: Check signs, plan, signal, scan, slow
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: For a turn, watch for turn signs and signals, plan ahead, signal before you reach the turn, look front, back and both sides, and adjust your speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Where U-turns are permitted in Maryland, how do you signal, yield, and choose your finishing lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: U-turns are dangerous and not legal everywhere; where allowed, signal left, stop and yield to oncoming traffic, then turn into the outside, right-hand lane going the other way.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: Along stretches posted with Stay Right signs, when is leaving the right-hand lane allowed?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Where stay right signs are posted, drive in the right-hand lane or lanes except when passing.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Which blinker starts a legal Maryland U-turn, and why watch which opposite lane you finish in?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: A U-turn is signaled with the left turn signal and ends in the outside, right-hand lane of the opposite direction, not the lane nearest the center.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What steps come before passing, and what exact mirror sight confirms it is safe to merge back?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Before passing, judge the time and space needed, signal, pass at a safe distance, and return to your lane only when both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rear-view mirror.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Which side is standard for passing, and under what conditions is passing on the right legal?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Pass on the left as a rule; passing on the right is allowed only when safe and on the road, when the other vehicle is turning left or you are on an unobstructed road or one-way road with two or more lanes in your direction.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: What two obligations fall on you whenever another motorist is overtaking your vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: When another vehicle is passing you, you must yield and must not speed up.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Contrast the duty of the driver being passed with the duty of the overtaking driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: The driver being passed must yield and hold speed, while the passing driver must signal and wait for both headlights in the mirror before moving back.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Even when a car ahead is waiting to turn left, may you ever leave the road onto the shoulder to pass?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Passing on the right is an exception allowed only when it is safe, you stay on the road, and the other vehicle is turning left or you are on an unobstructed road with two or more lanes your way; it is never allowed on the shoulder.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Which four zone, center-line, or traffic conditions bar you from overtaking?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: Do not pass in a no-passing zone, where the solid yellow center line is on your side, at double solid yellow lines, or when passing would interfere with other vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: Where do hilltops, curves, bridges, elevated roads, and tunnels make passing illegal?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Do not pass near the top of a hill or on a curve where you cannot see ahead, or with a blocked view within one hundred feet of a bridge, elevated road or tunnel.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Within what distance of intersections or railroad grade crossings is passing banned, alongside shoulders?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Do not pass while crossing or within one hundred feet of an intersection or railroad grade crossing, and never pass on the shoulder on either side.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How does Maryland's hundred-foot no-passing rule at intersections and tracks differ from bridges and tunnels?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: The one hundred-foot no-passing distance applies to intersections and railroad grade crossings always, but to bridges, elevated roads and tunnels only when your view is blocked.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: How does a single solid yellow center line differ from double solid yellow lines for passing?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A single solid yellow center line bans passing when it is on your side of the road, while double solid yellow lines ban passing wherever they appear.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: What three visual features let a driver recognize any road message quickly at highway speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Traffic signs speak through symbols and words, and a driver should recognize each one fast from its shape, its color and the words, numbers or symbols printed on it.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What quick clue do you get just from spotting a panel's main background color down the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: The main background color of a sign is a quick clue to the kind of information the sign carries.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What four urgent commands or warnings does a red background communicate to drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: A red sign tells you to stop, to yield, not to enter, or that you are going the wrong way.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What broad category of information does a standard yellow background deliver to approaching drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: A yellow sign gives a general warning about what lies ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: What specific roadside environment is announced whenever you spot an orange background?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: An orange sign warns of a construction or maintenance work area.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Which three vulnerable road-user groups are protected by fluorescent yellow-green panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school, pedestrian and bicycle signs.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Alongside turn bans and Left Turn Only, which five classic restriction messages appear in the manual's regulatory set?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Regulatory examples in the manual include signs that ban right turns, left turns, U-turns or all turns, plus Left Turn Only, Do Not Enter, Wrong Way, No Parking, No Turn on Red and Do Not Pass.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: What four lane, median, left-turn, and parking rules appear among the manual's additional regulatory examples?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Further regulatory examples tell you to keep right of a median, to yield on a green light when turning left, that a lane is a bike lane, or that parking is reserved for disability permit holders.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How do standard yellow, orange, and fluorescent yellow-green divide up warning duties on the road?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Yellow is a general warning, orange warns of construction or maintenance work, and fluorescent yellow-green is reserved for school, pedestrian and bicycle signs.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Which three types of roadway rules or guidance appear on white backgrounds?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: White is used for speed limit signs, keep right signs and some guide signs.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What three pieces of navigation help do green highway boards give drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: A green sign shows destinations, distances and directions.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What roadside needs are pointed out by blue highway panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: A blue sign points to services such as food, gas and rest areas.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: What two kinds of destinations are marked by brown roadside panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: A brown sign marks recreation areas and places of cultural interest.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What sudden roadside situation is marked with fluorescent pink panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Fluorescent pink is used for signs at emergency traffic incidents.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which two kinds of roadway displays use a black background?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Black is the color of One Way signs and of signs whose messages change.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How do green, blue, and brown highway boards split up navigation information for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Green guides you with destinations, distances and directions, blue points to services, and brown marks recreation and cultural interest areas.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What geometry has eight sides on the road, and what exact vehicle action does it always demand?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: An octagon, the eight-sided shape, always means stop, and you must bring the vehicle to a complete stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What command does a downward-pointing triangle give, and how must you handle crossing traffic and walkers?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: A triangle means yield: slow down and stop if you need to so that other vehicles and pedestrians get the right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What lies ahead when you spot a diamond outline, and how should you prepare to respond?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A diamond-shaped sign warns of special conditions or hazards ahead, so be ready to slow down and react.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What zone starts where a pennant-shaped panel stands, and what maneuver is banned there?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no passing zone begins, and you must not pass other vehicles there.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What two child-safety locations are marked by a five-sided pentagon outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A pentagon, the five-sided shape, warns of a school zone and marks a school crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: What specific hazard up ahead is announced exclusively by a round roadside outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: A round sign gives warning that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Where does a white X-shaped crossbuck stand, and what exact spot does it pinpoint?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A crossbuck sign stands at a highway-rail grade crossing to show exactly where the railroad crossing is.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which road command owns the sole eight-sided outline on the highway, and what are its letter and background colors?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: The stop sign, white letters on red, is the only eight-sided sign you will meet on the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Which road command owns the sole three-sided outline, and how are its letters and background colored?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: The yield sign, red letters on white, is the only sign with its three-sided shape.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do stop and yield panels contrast in both their exclusive side counts and their color schemes?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign and uses white letters on red, while the yield sign is the only three-sided sign and uses red letters on white.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does the braking requirement for an octagon differ from the braking requirement for a triangle?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: An octagon always demands a complete stop, whereas a triangle asks you to slow down and stop only if needed to give others the right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does a circular railroad panel differ in placement and role from a crossbuck?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A round sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead, while a crossbuck marks the crossing location itself.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: What separates the meaning of a diamond, a pennant, and a five-sided pentagon?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: A diamond warns of hazards ahead, a pennant marks the start of a no passing zone, and a pentagon signals a school zone or school crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How does the usual message of a vertical rectangle differ from that of a horizontal rectangle?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Rectangles are regulatory or guide signs: a vertical one usually states an instruction or rule of the road, while a horizontal one usually gives directions or information.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What three recreational or route destinations are marked by a trapezoid outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: A trapezoid sign marks recreation and cultural interest areas and National Forest Routes.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: What do regulatory panels state, and are drivers legally required to follow them?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Regulatory signs state traffic laws, and you are required to obey them.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: What color and geometry regulate traffic speeds, and what exact limit does a speed limit board set?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Rectangular four-sided signs with black lettering on white regulate traffic, and the speed limit sign among them gives the maximum speed for the stretch of road where it stands.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: When comparing two rectangular road boards, what tells you one states a rule while the other gives directions?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: A vertical rectangle usually gives a rule or instruction, while a horizontal rectangle usually gives directions or information.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Where exact three places, in fallback order, must you halt your wheels at a posted stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop completely at the stop line; with no stop line, stop before the crosswalk; with neither, stop before you enter the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Once you make a full stop at a stop post, whom must you yield to and how long must you wait?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: After stopping at a stop sign, yield to the vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection and stay stopped until you can safely enter and go through.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: What step-by-step routine must you follow as you roll toward a yield post?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Approaching a yield sign, slow down, look left and right, and yield to pedestrians, bicycles and vehicles, then go on only when it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What maneuver does a Two-way Left panel authorize for traffic flowing from both directions?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: A Two-way Left sign means drivers coming from either direction may use the center lane to make a left turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What restriction does a One Way panel place on every lane of that roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: A One Way sign means traffic may move only in the direction its arrow points.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: What requirement must your car meet before you enter a High Occupancy Vehicle lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: A High Occupancy Vehicle lane may be used only when your vehicle carries the number of people marked on its sign.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How does traffic movement under a Two-way Left panel contrast with movement under a One Way panel?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A Two-way Left sign lets traffic from both directions use the center lane for left turns, while a One Way sign allows travel only in the arrow's direction.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Why do highway engineers place warning panels upstream of certain road features?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Warning signs give road users notice of a situation that may not be easy to see in time.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Which three advance warning panels alert you that a mandatory traffic control sits just around the bend?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Some warning signs announce a control device before you reach it, such as Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead and Signal Ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: Which five specific construction-zone warnings are highlighted in the manual's work-area section?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: Work-area warnings include Flagger Ahead, Roadwork Ahead, Detour, Begin Work Zone and End Active Work Zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: What penalty warning accompanies the manual's work-zone panel that activates when its beacons flash?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: A sign stating that a work zone is active when its lights flash is labeled in the manual with a note that fines are increased.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: What five alignment or grade changes do road-shape warning panels preview for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: Warning signs also flag the shape of the road, including a sharp right turn, curves, sharp turns, a steep hill and a side road entering ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: What four lane-drop, merge, or median transitions do lane-change warning panels announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Other warning signs tell you that lanes or roads are changing: a lane ends and you merge left, two roads merge, the road divides ahead, or a divided road ends ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: Which four junction layouts—including roundabouts and rail-adjacent corners—appear in the manual's intersection warning set?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: Intersection warnings in the manual include a general intersection sign, a "T" intersection ahead, a traffic circle or roundabout, and a railroad before a "T" intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: Which five groups of people, vehicles, or animals are covered by the manual's crossing warning panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: Crossing warnings cover pedestrians, trails, pedestrians with bicycles, trucks, and deer or other wildlife.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: Alongside alignment and crossing alerts, which traction warning and passing restriction appear in the manual's warning set?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: The warning sign set in the manual also shows a Slippery When Wet sign and a No Passing Zone sign.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Which two advance alerts warn drivers about students walking or boarding ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: School warnings include a School Crossing Ahead sign and a School Bus Stop Ahead sign.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: Where are overhead lane-use boards mounted, and what three things do they tell drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: Overhead lane use signs are mounted above the road and tell you about destinations, directions and how to use each lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: What two pieces of highway identity are displayed together on a route marker shield?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: Some roads carry route numbers, and route marker signs show both the route number and the kind of road, such as a U.S. route or a state route.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: How do service information and guide boards help travelers choose highway exits?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: Service information and guide signs tell you which businesses and services you can reach by taking certain exits.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.front: Which seven traveler facilities and transit hubs appear among the manual's service and guide examples?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.expected_back: Examples of service and guide signs in the manual point to lodging, a hospital, gas, food, an airport, a train station and a park and ride lot.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.front: At what exact interval are mile marker posts placed along interstate highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.expected_back: Mile marker signs stand at every mile along interstate highways.

sec05-card-sec05-F49.front: Why should you note the nearest mile marker number if a crash or breakdown strands you on the highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F49.expected_back: A mile marker tells you where you are, so you can guide a tow truck or emergency personnel to your location.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What letter class designates Maryland's noncommercial license for ordinary cars, vans, and pickup trucks?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: A noncommercial driver's license lets you drive ordinary vehicles such as cars, pickup trucks and vans, and it is also known as a Class C license.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: How do you begin a Maryland license application at the MVA, and what age-and-name document do you bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: To apply, you book an appointment at any MVA branch and bring proof of age showing your full name, such as a birth certificate or passport.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Alongside lawful-status and Social Security proof, how many Maryland residency documents must you bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: You also bring proof of lawful status if you were born outside the United States, your Social Security Number or proof you are not eligible for one, and two documents proving Maryland residence.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which document versions does the MVA accept, and which three kinds get turned away?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Documents must be originals or copies certified by the agency that issued them; the MVA rejects photocopies, notarized copies and any document with altered or erased information.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which education course must every Maryland permit holder younger than twenty-five finish, and who must teach it?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: While holding the permit, an applicant under twenty-five must complete the Maryland Driver Education Program taught by an MVA-approved school.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: In what official record does every permit holder track supervised driving time, and where can you download a copy?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Every permit holder records practice hours in a Practice and Skills Log, which is available on the MVA website.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which permit type is built for someone never previously licensed, how long does it last, and what tests unlock it?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A first-time driver needs a Type one Learner's Instructional Permit, which is valid for up to two years and requires passing the vision screening and the knowledge test.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Who uses a Type two learner's permit, and what minimum age, validity cap, and wait period apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A Type two Learner's Instructional Permit is for someone who already holds a license and wants a different class; you must be at least sixteen years and six months old, it lasts up to one hundred eighty days, and you may take the driving test after holding it at least fourteen days.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What personal factor sets your permit holding period before a Provisional License, and what term names a permit seeker?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: How long you must hold the permit before a Provisional License depends on your age, and a person applying for a permit is called an applicant.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Contrast who needs a Type one permit versus a Type two permit and how long each stays valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A Type one permit is for someone who has never been licensed and lasts up to two years, while a Type two permit is for a licensed driver changing class and lasts up to one hundred eighty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: How old must a Maryland applicant under twenty-five be to apply for a learner's permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Permit applicants younger than twenty-five must be at least fifteen years and nine months old.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How many total and nighttime supervised hours must an applicant under twenty-five log, and how is night defined?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: An applicant under twenty-five must log at least sixty practice hours with a supervising driver, with at least ten of them driven between thirty minutes before sunset and thirty minutes after sunrise.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What driver-ed and supervised-hour totals, including night hours, apply to a permit holder aged twenty-five or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.memory_hook: Driver ed, fourteen total, three night
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: An applicant aged twenty-five or older must complete the Maryland Driver Education Program and at least fourteen practice hours with a supervising driver, at least three of them in the night window from thirty minutes before sunset to thirty minutes after sunrise.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: At least how many days must an applicant aged twenty-five or older hold their learner's permit before Provisional?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: An applicant aged twenty-five or older must hold the permit for at least forty-five days before becoming eligible for a Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How does the minimum age for a first-time permit under twenty-five compare with the Type two permit minimum?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The minimum permit age for applicants under twenty-five is fifteen years and nine months, which differs from the Type two permit minimum of sixteen years and six months.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Compare total and nighttime supervised practice hours for learners under twenty-five against learners twenty-five and up?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Supervised practice is sixty hours with ten at night for applicants under twenty-five, but fourteen hours with three at night for applicants twenty-five and older.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Alongside a parent or guardian co-signer under eighteen, what extra school form must an applicant under sixteen submit?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs a parent or legal guardian to co-sign, and an applicant under sixteen must also hand in a completed Learner's Permit School Attendance Certification form (DL-three hundred).

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Who counts as a minor in Maryland licensing, who normally co-signs, and what documents prove that relationship?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Anyone under eighteen is a minor and needs a parent or legal guardian to co-sign, with proof such as an original or certified birth certificate naming the parent or court guardianship papers.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: When may an adult spouse or a responsible adult like an employer co-sign a minor's license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A married minor's spouse who is eighteen or older may co-sign with proof of marriage, and a minor with no parent, guardian or spouse may use a responsible adult, such as an employer, with proof like parents' death certificates or emancipation papers.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: How can a co-signer revoke a minor's Maryland license, and how long does that cancellation stay in place?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: A co-signer can cancel a minor's license by written request to the MVA's Administrative Adjudication Division, and it stays canceled until age eighteen unless a qualified co-signer signs a new application.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: In what priority order does Maryland allow parents, spouses, or responsible adults like employers to co-sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: A parent or guardian is the normal co-signer for a minor, a spouse aged eighteen or older may co-sign for a married minor, and a responsible adult such as an employer is allowed only when none of those exists.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: At any age, what happens to your permit wait after a moving-violation conviction, PBJ, or any suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: At any age, a conviction or Probation Before Judgment (PBJ) for a moving violation, or a suspension for any reason, means holding the permit at least nine months after the latest such date.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: How many violation-free months must a permit holder younger than eighteen complete before Provisional?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: A permit holder under eighteen must hold the permit for at least nine months with no violation before qualifying for a Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: How long must an eighteen-year-old graduate or someone aged nineteen to twenty-four hold a clean permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A permit holder who is eighteen with a high school diploma or GED, or who is nineteen to twenty-four, must hold the permit at least three months with no violation before qualifying for a Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Line up Maryland's three clean-permit holding periods across under-eighteen, nineteen-to-twenty-four, and twenty-five-plus?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.memory_hook: Nine months, three months, forty-five days
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: The violation-free holding period is nine months for a permit holder under eighteen but three months for an eighteen-year-old with a diploma or GED or anyone aged nineteen to twenty-four, and forty-five days applies to applicants twenty-five and older.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does the nine-month violation or suspension clock interact with shorter adult permit minimums?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: A moving-violation conviction, a PBJ or a suspension sets a nine-month holding period counted from the latest such date at any age, which is separate from the age-based minimums.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Who enters the Provisional License stage, and what mix of solo freedom and limits comes with it?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: A Provisional License goes to new drivers who have never been licensed and allows unsupervised driving with restrictions, such as no passengers and no night driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: At least how long must you hold a Maryland Provisional License before advancing to a regular license?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: You keep the Provisional License for at least eighteen months before you can qualify for a regular Driver's License.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What education, permit validity, and driving-record rules must be satisfied to earn a Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: To move up to a Provisional License you need a completed approved driver education program, a valid unexpired permit held violation-free for the required time, and no moving-violation conviction or PBJ in that period.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What signed paperwork and practical exam complete your upgrade from learner's permit to Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: You must also turn in a signed Practice and Skills Log showing at least sixty supervised practice hours, or fourteen if you are twenty-five or older, and pass the driving skills test.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What minimum birthday, Provisional time, and clean-record window unlock Maryland's final Driver's License?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: The Driver's License is the final stage of the graduated system and requires being at least eighteen, holding a Provisional License for at least eighteen months, and no moving-violation conviction or PBJ within the past eighteen months.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: How does the MVA issue your upgrade from Provisional to full Driver's License, and what must you carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Once you qualify, the MVA converts your Provisional License to a Driver's License automatically and mails a card that you must carry together with the Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: What is the core supervision difference between driving on a learner's permit and driving on a Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The permit stage requires a supervising driver in the car, whereas the provisional stage allows driving alone but with restrictions such as no passengers and no night driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: What three eighteen-based benchmarks must all align before a Provisional holder earns a full license?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: The full Driver's License needs three things at once: age eighteen or older, at least eighteen months on the Provisional License, and a clean moving-violation record for the past eighteen months.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: When your full-license conversion card arrives in the mail, does it replace your Provisional card?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Graduation to the full license happens automatically by mail, and the mailed card is carried together with the Provisional License rather than replacing it.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What three tests and special course must someone holding a license from another country complete in Maryland?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: A driver licensed in another country must pass the vision screening, knowledge test and skills test and complete an MVA-approved three-hour roadway safety driving education program.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: If an out-of-country license is not printed in English, what companion document or translation sources qualify?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: A foreign license not in English also needs an International License or an English translation prepared on the letterhead of an MVA-approved provider, a court translator or the country's embassy.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Which three contact and verification details must appear on any translated license document?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: A translated document must show the translator's typed or printed name, telephone number and signature.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: When the knowledge test already exists in your language, how many attempts come before using an interpreter?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: If the knowledge test is offered in your language, you must attempt it at least five times before you may use an interpreter.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Who covers interpreter costs at the MVA, and what credentials must that interpreter hold?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: The MVA charges no fee for using an interpreter, but you pay the interpreter, who must be on the approved list and show a valid photo license or ID card.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What kinds of testing accommodations can applicants with disabilities receive, and how are they tailored?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Applicants with disabilities can get test accommodations such as extra time, sign language support, oral testing, screen readers, headphones and visual aids, based on each person's needs.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: What optional card can a driver with a developmental disability pick up at an MVA desk, and is proof required?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: A driver with a developmental disability may choose to carry a blue, license-sized Developmental Disability Disclosure Card, available at any MVA information desk without documenting the disability.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Combine Maryland's fee policy and supported-language attempt rule for using a test interpreter?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.memory_hook: No MVA fee, self-paid, five tries
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Using an interpreter is free at the MVA, yet the interpreter's own services are paid by you, and in a language the test is offered in you need at least five attempts first.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What safety advantage do painted roadway lines give you compared with roadside posts?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Pavement markings are lines painted on the road that guide and inform you without making you take your eyes off the roadway.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Why do highway crews paint certain stripes extra wide or add raised reflective markers?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.memory_hook: Extra width and reflectors grab eyes
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: In some places lines are made extra wide or fitted with reflective markers so they catch your attention and are easier to see.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Compared with roads posted at forty-five or fifty miles per hour, how deadly are crashes at sixty-five or higher?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Citing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the manual says a crash where the limit is sixty-five miles per hour or more is over twice as likely to be fatal as one where the limit is forty-five or fifty miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Compared with roads posted at forty miles per hour or less, how likely is a crash at sixty-five or higher to be fatal?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: The same NHTSA comparison says a crash on a road posted at sixty-five miles per hour or more is nearly five times as likely to be fatal as one on a road posted at forty miles per hour or less.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: What single habit does more than anything else to prevent death or severe injury in every seat on every trip?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: According to the manual, no single step does more to keep you from being killed or badly hurt in a crash than wearing a seat belt, on every trip and in front or back seats.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Roughly what percentage of Maryland riders buckle up today, and what target has the state set?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: About ninety percent of Maryland drivers and passengers buckle up, and the state's stated goal is one hundred percent.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: About how many seconds does latching a seat belt take, and what could it prevent for most unbelted crash victims?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Buckling up takes about three seconds, and the manual says most injuries and deaths among unbelted crash victims could have been avoided by wearing a belt.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How do the two fatal-crash risk multiples compare as the gap widens below sixty-five miles per hour?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: The fatal-crash comparison grows with the gap in posted limits: over twice as deadly against roads posted at forty-five or fifty miles per hour, and nearly five times against roads posted at forty miles per hour or less.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: What traffic flow does a single broken white line separate, and may you cross it to switch lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: A single broken white line divides lanes carrying traffic the same way on roads with more than one lane, and you may cross it to change lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What directions of traffic does a single broken yellow center line divide, and what passing rule applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: A single broken yellow line divides traffic moving in opposite directions and allows careful passing from either side; it serves as the center line on two-lane, two-way roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What two boundary or lane-separation jobs can a single solid white line perform?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: A single solid white line marks the right edge of the road and can also divide same-direction lanes where changing lanes is discouraged.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What rule applies where double solid white lines run side by side between same-direction lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Double solid white lines side by side divide same-direction lanes where lane changes are not allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does lane-changing permission step down from broken white to single solid white to double solid white?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: A broken white line lets you change lanes between same-direction lanes, a single solid white line discourages it, and double solid white lines prohibit it.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How do solid white and solid yellow edge lines help you tell your right road edge from your left edge?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of a road, but a solid yellow line marks the left edge of divided highways, one-way roads and ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How does passing permission on a single broken yellow center line compare with double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A single broken yellow center line allows careful passing from both sides, while double solid yellow lines forbid passing from both sides.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: On divided highways, one-way streets, and ramps, which border of the roadway carries a single solid yellow line?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: A single solid yellow line marks the left edge of divided highways, one-way roads and ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What physical separation between opposing lanes makes a roadway an official divided highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: A divided highway is one with a guardrail, a strip of land or some other barrier between the two directions of traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Beyond banning routine lane shifts, what special lane type or roadway hazard can double solid white lines outline?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Double solid white lines may also set general lanes apart from HOV lanes, or appear ahead of an obstruction you are allowed to pass on either side.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What special lane is framed by double broken yellow lines, and what controls when you may use it?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Double broken yellow lines side by side mark the edges of a reversible lane, and you enter or leave that lane only as its signs and signals permit.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: How are the solid and broken yellow stripes arranged along each side of a two-way left-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Solid-plus-broken yellow lines also outline a two-way left turn lane, with the solid lines on the outside and the broken lines on the inside.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How can you tell a reversible lane apart from a two-way left-turn lane purely from yellow edge stripes?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Double broken yellow lines outline a reversible lane, while solid outer lines with broken inner lines outline a two-way left turn lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What traffic flow do double solid yellow lines separate, and who is allowed to pass across them?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines divide opposing traffic and forbid passing from either direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Even though passing is banned, when are you legally allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: You are allowed to turn left across double solid yellow lines, for example to pull into a driveway.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: On what kind of roadway do engineers paint one solid yellow stripe right beside one broken yellow stripe?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line is used on two-way roads where passing is allowed in only one direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Along a mixed solid-and-broken yellow center line, which lane may pass carefully and which must hold back?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: With a solid-plus-broken yellow pair, drivers on the broken-line side may pass carefully, while drivers on the solid-line side may not pass.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: What simple visual check tells you instantly whether passing is legal alongside a mixed yellow center pair?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: With a solid line next to a broken yellow line, the rule depends on which line is nearer to you: broken on your side means you may pass with care, solid on your side means you may not.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How do double solid yellow lines treat overtaking a slow car compared with turning left into an entrance?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines bar passing, yet a left turn across them, such as into a driveway, is still allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What three pieces of lane guidance or upcoming road changes can painted pavement words and symbols communicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Word and symbol markings on the pavement tell you how to use a lane, which direction to travel, and when a lane reduction is coming, such as two lanes narrowing to one.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What do directional arrows and word messages painted inside a lane tell drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Arrows and other word messages painted in a lane show how you are allowed to move from that lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What two sensitive zones lie ahead when giant school words or railroad crossing letters are painted on your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: SCHOOL and RxR painted on the road warn that you are nearing a school area or a railroad crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What does a solid white bar painted across your lane show at a stop post or red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: A stop line is a solid white line showing where you must stop for a STOP sign or a red traffic signal.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: What row of painted shapes marks a yield line, and what must you do there?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Yield lines are rows of small triangles painted across a lane that show where you must yield to vehicles or pedestrians.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: How are pedestrian crosswalks marked on the pavement, and how can their stripe pattern vary?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Crosswalk lines are solid white lines marking where pedestrians cross, and some crosswalks add lines between them or use other lines instead.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: How can you distinguish a stop line from yield lines by looking at the shapes painted across your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: A stop line is a single solid white line marking where to stop, while yield lines are rows of small triangles marking where to yield.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Do most Maryland roadways where cyclists and drivers share space have special bike paint or posts?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Most Maryland roads that bicycles share with motor vehicles carry no special signs or pavement markings for bicycles.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Where do shared-use lane symbols mostly appear, and what three safety jobs do they serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Shared-use lane markings, found mostly in cities, warn drivers that cyclists may be present, show cyclists where to ride, and discourage riding against traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: How are bicycle-only lanes separated from motor vehicle travel lanes and identified on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Bicycle-only lanes are separated from motor vehicle lanes by solid or broken white lines and may be marked with bike lane signs or bicycle symbols and arrows.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Where street parallel parking is allowed alongside a bike lane, how are those two spaces divided?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Where parallel parking is permitted, similar lines may separate a bike lane from the parking lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: How does lane space under shared-use markings differ from a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Shared-use lane markings mean cyclists and drivers share a lane, whereas a bike lane is set apart for bicycles by solid or broken white lines.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Who holds the right-of-way at street crossings, and must pedestrians obey traffic signals too?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at street crossings, but they too must obey traffic control signals.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: At a crossing without traffic signals, when must you stop for a pedestrian—only on painted stripes or unmarked corners too?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Where there is no traffic signal, you must stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk whether it is marked or unmarked.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which three groups of pedestrians need extra alertness and crossing time from drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Watch especially for deaf, blind or mobility-impaired pedestrians, who may not see or hear traffic well and may need more time to cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Do intersections without painted lines still have legal crosswalks where drivers must stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: A crosswalk is where pedestrians may cross and drivers must stop for them; some are painted, others are not, and most intersections have one even without markings.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What is Maryland's strict rule when another vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: You may not pass any vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: During which two signal turns must you yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: You must yield to pedestrians when turning on green and when making a permitted turn on red after stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: When do police cars, fire engines, and ambulances hold the legal right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Police cars, ambulances and fire engines have the right-of-way when their sirens and flashing lights are on.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: What three steps must you take the instant you see or hear a signaling emergency vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: As soon as you see or hear an emergency vehicle signaling, get as close to the road edge as you can, keep out of intersections and stay stopped until it passes.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: Under what two rare exceptions may you pass an emergency vehicle running signals in your direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: You may not pass an emergency vehicle using its signals in your direction unless it stops or a police officer directs you to pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What does Maryland's Move-Over rule require when approaching a stopped emergency, tow, or service vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck or other service vehicle, move to a lane not right next to it; if you cannot, slow to a safe speed and be ready to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does your legal duty for a moving emergency vehicle differ from a stopped one on the shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: For a moving emergency vehicle you pull to the edge and stop, but for a stopped one you move to a lane not next to it or slow and be ready to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How do large trucks handle intersection turns differently from passenger cars, especially before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Trucks need more room than cars and swing wide at intersections, often moving left before a right turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: When a truck ahead drifts left near an intersection, why should you hold back before passing on its right?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Passing a truck on its right is risky, so wait to see whether a truck that drifts left is about to turn right before you pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What happens if you try to squeeze along the right side of a truck starting an intersection turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Never squeeze along the right side of a truck starting a turn at an intersection, or you may be trapped between it and the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How should you pass a truck moving in your direction, and what mirror check clears you to merge back?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Pass a same-direction truck quickly, and return to its lane only once both of its headlights show in your rear-view mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: How does creeping past a painted intersection stop line create a collision risk with large trucks?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Stopping beyond a stop line can put your vehicle in the path of trucks turning from the cross street.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How does a loaded truck's weight compare with a typical car's, and how much stopping room can that rig need?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Never cut in front of a truck: a fully loaded one can top eighty thousand pounds and need a football field's length to stop, while most cars weigh only two thousand pounds.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How many major blind spots surround a large truck, and what term does the manual use for them?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Trucks have four large blind spots, called no-zones, where other vehicles vanish from the driver's view.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: How can you tell instantly whether you are sitting inside a truck or bus's side no-zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Side no-zones lie on both sides of trucks and buses; if you cannot see the driver's face in the side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: How long and how wide is a large truck's right-side blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: A truck's right-side blind spot runs the full length of the trailer and reaches out three lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What two dangers make tailgating behind a truck or bus especially hazardous?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Trucks and buses have huge rear no-zones, so do not tailgate them; the driver cannot see you and you have no escape if they stop suddenly.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: Compared with passenger cars, how much time and distance do trucks and buses need to stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Truck and bus drivers need nearly twice the time and room that cars need to stop, so do not pull in front of them too soon after passing.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: After passing a truck or bus and seeing both headlights in your mirror, what must you avoid doing once in front?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: After passing a truck or bus, wait until both of its headlights appear in your rear-view mirror before moving in front, and then do not slow down.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Why must you never walk or drive behind a truck that is backing up?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Never cross behind a backing truck; its driver has no rear-view mirror, and hundreds of people are killed or hurt each year this way.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What quick visual rule keeps you out of a truck's side, rear, and front no-zones?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Each truck no-zone has its own rule: beside a truck, make sure you can see the driver's face in the mirror; behind it, do not tailgate; in front, do not cut in until both headlights show in your mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How many feet away must you stop when approaching a school bus with flashing red lights from behind or ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: When a school bus stops with flashing red lights, stop at least twenty feet from its back if you are behind it, or twenty feet from its front if you are ahead of it.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Which two cues allow you to start moving again after stopping for a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Stay stopped until the school bus moves again or switches off its flashing red lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: When are oncoming drivers NOT required to stop for a school bus flashing red lights on a multi-lane road?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: On a multi-lane road split by a physical barrier, you do not stop for a school bus on the far side of the barrier.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: How do motorcyclists' road rights compare with car drivers', and how much higher is their crash injury risk?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Motorcyclists share the same rights and privileges as other drivers, yet are six times more likely than car drivers to be hurt in a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Why must left-turning drivers look extra hard for oncoming motorcycles, and who is usually at fault in car-motorcycle crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Yield to an oncoming motorcycle when you turn left; failing to can bring a citation with significant penalties, and drivers are at fault in over half of car-motorcycle crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What two-step visual check should you make before changing lanes or merging, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Look twice, using mirrors and a shoulder check, before merging or changing lanes, because a small motorcycle can hide in a blind spot.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Why must you never squeeze beside a motorcycle in the same lane, even when the rider hugs one side?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Never share a lane with a motorcycle; riders may use the whole lane and shift within it to avoid hazards, handle wind and be seen.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Keep a following distance of at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle, since riders may slow without brake lights showing.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: How do you safely complete a pass around a motorcycle, and what should you do when a rider passes you?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: When passing a motorcycle leave plenty of room, and pull back in only once its headlight shows in your rear-view mirror; if a rider passes you, hold your speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: How should you handle signaling, merging, or speed around a group of motorcyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: Near a group of riders, signal early and wait for room, merge between riders only with enough safe space, and for a small group consider slowing to let it pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: How does Maryland law classify bicycles on public roads, and what rules apply to riders?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Maryland law treats bicycles as vehicles; cyclists may use the road and must obey all traffic signals.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: Which three traits make bicyclists vulnerable to severe injury or death from minor driver errors?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: Cyclists are harder to see, quieter and unprotected by a vehicle body, so even a small driver mistake can seriously injure or kill one.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: Where are bicycles prohibited in Maryland, and where else should you expect them anytime?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: Expect cyclists on every kind of road except interstates and tolled bridges and tunnels, at intersections and circles, in any weather and at any hour.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Why is riding near the center of the travel lane often safest for a cyclist along narrow roads or parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: Cyclists may ride in the travel lane for safety on narrow roads or to avoid hazards, and with no shoulder or with parked cars on the right the lane center is often safest.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: When does Maryland law allow a slow-moving bicyclist to occupy the entire travel lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: In Maryland a cyclist may take the full lane even well below traffic speed when the lane is too narrow for a vehicle to pass the bicycle safely within it.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: What check must you perform every time before swinging open a parked car's door?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: Check for cyclists coming from behind before you open a car door.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: What is Maryland's statewide default rule on sidewalk bicycling, whom must riders yield to, and who can restrict it?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: Bicycles may ride on sidewalks statewide, yielding to pedestrians and mobility-device users, though local governments can ban sidewalk riding.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: Who holds the right-of-way when your motor vehicle turns or enters and crosses a bike lane or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: Cyclists have the right-of-way when a motor vehicle turns, and you must yield to cyclists in a bike lane or shoulder you enter or cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: What right-of-way do bicycles hold inside crosswalks, and what penalties hit if failing to yield causes a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: In a crosswalk a bicycle has the same right-of-way as a pedestrian, and failing to yield to a bicycle in a way that causes a crash brings fines and or prison time plus points.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: How should you adjust speed approaching a cyclist, and why should you keep off the horn?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: Slow down approaching a cyclist and do not honk, because a loud noise can startle the rider into a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.front: How do bicyclists communicate turns, and why must you avoid following closely behind one?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.expected_back: Cyclists use hand and arm signals since bicycles lack turn signals, and they may swerve or change speed suddenly to avoid holes or glass, so do not follow closely.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.front: What minimum clearance must you leave when passing any bicyclist, regardless of whether they ride in a bike lane or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.expected_back: Pass a cyclist as you would any slow vehicle, waiting for oncoming traffic to clear and leaving at least three feet, whether the bike is in a bike lane, on the shoulder or in your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.front: After overtaking a bicyclist, what visual check confirms you have enough space to move back right?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.expected_back: After passing a cyclist, see the bicycle in your rear-view mirror before moving back into your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F48.front: Up to what speed can experienced cyclists travel, and what visual trap should drivers watch for?
sec09-card-sec09-F48.expected_back: Experienced cyclists can ride as fast as thirty-five miles per hour and may be closer than they seem.

sec09-card-sec09-F52.front: What move should you expect from a shoulder cyclist approaching a narrow bridge or row of parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F52.expected_back: Where a bridge, parked cars or another obstruction narrows the road, expect a shoulder cyclist to merge left into the travel lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F53.front: What might a faint reflective glint ahead at night turn out to be, and which beams should you use near a cyclist?
sec09-card-sec09-F53.expected_back: At night a faint reflective object may be a bicycle in the travel lane, so use low beams as you approach a cyclist.

sec09-card-sec09-F54.front: Which age group of cyclists is most likely to turn abruptly without warning, and how do you protect them?
sec09-card-sec09-F54.expected_back: Young cyclists are the most likely to change direction without warning, so obey school-zone and residential limits to give yourself time around them.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How do bicycle yield rules flip between intersection turns, crosswalks, and sidewalks?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.memory_hook: Cars yield crossings, sidewalk bikes yield
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A turning driver must yield to cyclists, and in a crosswalk a cyclist gets the same right-of-way as a pedestrian, whereas a cyclist riding on a sidewalk must yield to pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F47.front: What path should you assume an unsignaling cyclist will take at an intersection, and how do you cross trails?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.memory_hook: Assume straight, scan trails both ways
sec09-card-sec09-F47.expected_back: Assume a cyclist is going straight through an intersection unless the rider signals a turn, and look both ways before crossing a sidewalk or trail.

sec09-card-sec09-F49.front: What dangerous turn must you never make right after overtaking a bicycle on a shoulder or bike lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F49.expected_back: Never turn right from a through lane right after passing a bike on a shoulder or in a bike lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F50.front: How should you check and position your car before making a right turn where bikes may ride?
sec09-card-sec09-F50.expected_back: Before a right turn, check your right side and blind spot for bikes and move as far right as you can within the bike lane, shoulder or right turn lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F51.front: Which two intersection moves around left turns put oncoming or curbside cyclists in immediate danger?
sec09-card-sec09-F51.expected_back: Do not turn left directly in front of a bicycle, and look carefully for bikes before moving right to get around a left-turning vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F55.front: Must moped and motor-scooter operators obey standard traffic laws, and why do drivers miss them?
sec09-card-sec09-F55.expected_back: Moped and scooter riders must follow all traffic laws, and their small size makes them hard for other drivers to see.

sec09-card-sec09-F56.front: Which roads may mopeds and scooters use in Maryland, and where in the roadway do they ride?
sec09-card-sec09-F56.memory_hook: Posted fifty or less, keep right
sec09-card-sec09-F56.expected_back: Mopeds and scooters may use any road posted at fifty miles per hour or less, alone or side by side, on the road or shoulder, keeping as far right as is safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F57.front: What does ADAS stand for, and what share of crashes does the manual say proper use can prevent?
sec09-card-sec09-F57.expected_back: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, or ADAS, are safety features that the manual says prevent forty percent of crashes when used properly.

sec09-card-sec09-F58.front: Which three safety features does the manual list as ADAS examples, and how do they detect hazards?
sec09-card-sec09-F58.expected_back: Examples of ADAS are Automatic Emergency Braking, Lane Keeping Assistance and Blind Spot Warning, which use sensors and cameras to spot dangers.

sec09-card-sec09-F59.front: When driver-assistance tech is switched on, who remains legally and physically responsible for operating the vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F59.expected_back: Do not rely on ADAS to drive for you; you stay responsible for safe operation and for checking traffic with mirrors and cameras at all times.

sec09-card-sec09-F60.front: Under which weather and road shapes can ADAS struggle, and why can't you assume two brands work alike?
sec09-card-sec09-F60.expected_back: ADAS may not work properly in rain, snow, fog, on hills or around curves, and it behaves differently across vehicles with names that may not describe what it does.

sec09-card-sec09-F61.front: Which three maintenance and learning habits keep a vehicle's driver-assistance features working properly?
sec09-card-sec09-F61.expected_back: Keep sensors clean and undamaged, keep the software updated, and learn each vehicle's systems from its manual or the dealer.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: How do alcohol and drugs affect your driving capability, and whom do impaired drivers put at risk?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Alcohol and drugs impair driving, making it very hard or impossible to drive safely, and drunk or drugged driving threatens everyone on the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: What does BAC stand for, and what exact measurement does it describe?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, measures how much alcohol is in your blood.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Why can't you accurately estimate your BAC just by counting how many drinks you had?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: You cannot judge your BAC by counting drinks, because weight, body fat, and when and how much you ate change how your body handles alcohol.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Beyond body size and food, which three personal factors change how strongly alcohol hits your driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Fatigue, mood and medications also change how alcohol affects your driving.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: In which three zones around your vehicle must you maintain constant awareness to drive safely?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Safe driving needs constant awareness of the vehicles in front of, behind and beside you.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: At what Blood Alcohol Concentration does Maryland classify a driver as under the influence of alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Maryland treats a driver as under the influence of alcohol at a BAC of point zero eight or above.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Can you still face criminal charges in Maryland if your BAC tests below zero point zero eight?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Any amount of alcohol can hurt your driving: judgment and coordination may suffer well below point zero eight, which can still lead to criminal charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What three driving functions can suffer—and what happens to crash risk—after just a single drink?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Even one drink can affect your vision, simple movements and reaction time and raise your crash risk.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: How much alcohol may someone under age twenty-one legally consume in Maryland?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Drinking any alcohol at all is illegal for anyone under twenty-one.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What license actions and extra charge hit an under-twenty-one driver stopped after drinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one who is stopped after drinking will have the license suspended or revoked and may also be charged with breaking the license's alcohol restriction.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Where inside a motor vehicle is carrying an open alcohol container illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Driving with an open alcohol container in the passenger area of the vehicle is against the law.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What counts as an open container in Maryland, including when carrying a six-pack?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: An open container is any opened can, bottle, container or package, and a six-pack with open, empty or missing cans or bottles can count as one.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How does Maryland law define the passenger area for open-container rules?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: The passenger area covers the driver and passenger seats and any spot the driver or passengers can easily reach while seated.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How do Maryland's zero point zero eight standard, lower-BAC impairment rule, and under-twenty-one rule fit together?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: The legal under-the-influence line is a BAC of point zero eight, but impairment and criminal charges are possible at lower levels, and drivers under twenty-one may not drink any alcohol.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Does putting an open bottle off the seat cushion make it legal inside the cabin?
