sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: The open-container ban is tied to the passenger area, and that area is defined as the seats plus anywhere occupants can easily reach while sitting, not just the seats themselves.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Which three categories of non-alcohol substances can severely damage alertness, focus, coordination, and reaction time?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Illegal drugs, some prescription medicines and chemical inhalants can badly affect alertness, concentration, coordination and reaction time.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: What three road cues become harder to judge or respond to under the influence of any drug?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: All drugs can make it harder to judge distance and to respond to signals and sounds on the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What can happen to your Maryland license if you drive under the influence of controlled dangerous substances?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Driving under the influence of controlled dangerous substances can get your license suspended or revoked.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What warning should you check for on prescription and over-the-counter bottles, and what can ignoring it bring?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Read prescription and over-the-counter labels for warnings against driving or running heavy machinery; driving impaired against such a warning can bring a criminal charge.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How can having a child in the vehicle change the sentence for a drunk or drugged driving conviction?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: If you are convicted of drunk or drugged driving with a child in the vehicle, the judge may double your fine and jail time.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which six unsafe behaviors define aggressive driving in the Maryland manual?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Aggressive driving includes speeding, tailgating, ignoring signals and devices, unsafe lane changes, failing to yield and unsafe or illegal passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: Which five everyday trip pressures commonly push ordinary motorists into aggressive driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Crowded roads, surprise delays, hurrying, construction and stress can push people into driving aggressively.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What three mindset and scheduling habits help you avoid aggressive-driving flare-ups?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: To avoid aggressive-driving incidents, leave extra travel time, stay patient and courteous, and focus on your own driving.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Which four on-road courtesies keep traffic cooperative and defuse aggressive encounters?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Other anti-aggression habits are signaling what you plan to do, obeying all traffic controls, yielding the right-of-way and refusing to compete with other drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What simple everyday principle does the manual give for sharing the road with others?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: A useful rule is to treat other drivers and road users the way you want them to treat you.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which three faculties does distracted driving pull away from the road—and which one matters above all?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Distracted driving means taking your eyes, your hands or, above all, your mind off driving.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: Where does distracted driving rank among all causes of police-reported crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Distracted driving causes more police-reported crashes than any other cause.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: Beyond phones, what everyday cabin activities does the Maryland manual list as driving distractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Distractions include eating or drinking, adjusting music or a GPS, handling children or pets, loose objects, phone calls or texting, smoking, makeup, shaving, reading and talking with passengers.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What is Maryland's rule on holding a cell phone or texting while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving, texting included, is illegal, so you may not drive while holding your phone.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: May a Maryland driver under age eighteen talk on a hands-free Bluetooth phone, and what is the sole exception?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen may not use a cell phone at all while driving, even hands-free, except to call nine one one in an emergency.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How do Maryland's cell-phone rules contrast between drivers eighteen and older versus drivers under eighteen?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Drivers eighteen and older may use a phone hands-free, while drivers under eighteen may not use one at all except for a nine one one call, and no driver may use a hand-held phone.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Even though drivers eighteen and up may use hands-free devices, how often should they use the phone while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Adult drivers may make calls hands-free, but should keep phone use to a minimum.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What three safer habits should you use when a phone call needs to be made on a trip?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Safer phone habits are to call only in emergencies, let a passenger place the call when possible, or pull safely off the road and stop first.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What is the safest way to handle incoming phone calls and necessary conversations while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Let voicemail pick up incoming calls and keep any conversation short.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: Which three groups of motorists face an elevated risk of drowsy driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: People who drive many miles daily, people with sleep disorders and people on certain medicines face a higher risk of drowsiness.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: How does lack of sleep compare with alcohol or drugs in its effects on driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Lack of sleep slows reaction time, lowers awareness and impairs judgment much as drugs or alcohol do, sharply raising crash risk.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Which four physical or mental symptoms warn that drowsiness is taking over at the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Drowsiness warning signs include eyes closing or blurring, trouble holding your head up, nonstop yawning and drifting, disconnected thoughts.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Which four on-road mistakes reveal that you have grown dangerously drowsy?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: Other drowsiness signs are not recalling the last few miles, missing your exit, repeatedly leaving your lane and repeatedly changing speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: What is the best action to take the moment you feel tired or sleepy behind the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: If you get tired or sleepy at the wheel, the best response is to rest or switch drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Why does trying to push through drowsiness fail, and what actually solves it?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Drowsiness impairs judgment and reaction time much like alcohol, and the cure is rest or a new driver rather than pushing on.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: What fraction of fatal crashes does the Maryland manual's campaign page attribute to distracted driving, and what leads the list?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: The manual's campaign page states that one-third of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving, with cell phone use among the leading distractions.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: Roughly what scale of impaired-driving arrests happen on Maryland roads every year?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: Every year tens of thousands of people are arrested on Maryland roads for drunk or drugged driving.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: What two steps should you lock in before going out, and what financial and legal costs follow an impaired arrest?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: Before going out, plan a safe way home and name a sober driver, since an impaired-driving arrest brings large fines, possible jail and thousands of dollars in court costs.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Right after any collision, what two tools can you use to alert approaching traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: After any crash, switch on your emergency flashers or set out flares to warn other drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What is your duty to remain on site if a crash hurts anyone, including a walker or cyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: If anyone is hurt in a crash you are involved in, pedestrians and cyclists included, you must stay at the scene.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: When people are injured in a wreck, what must you report to nine one one and do with the cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: At an injury crash, call nine one one at once and report how many people are involved, what injuries they have and where the crash is, and leave the vehicles where they are.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Which three urgent crash conditions involving injuries, vehicle condition, or driver sobriety always require calling police?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: You must always call the police when someone is injured, when a vehicle cannot be moved, or when a driver seems to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Beyond injuries or impairment, which three other crash situations involving licensing, fleeing, or damaged property require calling police?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: You must also call the police when a driver has no license, when a driver tries to leave without giving insurance and other details, or when public property is damaged.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: During any roadside emergency, how should you handle the scene and why must your eyes stay on passing cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: In any roadside emergency, size up the situation, use good judgment and keep watching traffic, because conditions can change instantly.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does handling the vehicles after an injury crash compare with handling a drivable car when nobody is hurt?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: After an injury crash you leave the vehicles in place, but after an injury-free crash with a drivable vehicle you move it off the road near the crash spot.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What happens to your driver's license if you are convicted of fleeing a crash involving serious injury?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A conviction for leaving the scene of a crash with serious injury means your license is revoked.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Up to how much prison time and fine money can fleeing a serious-injury crash bring?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a serious-injury crash can also bring up to five years in prison and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: How does Maryland classify fleeing a fatal crash, and what are the maximum prison and fine penalties?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Leaving the scene of a crash in which someone dies is a felony punishable by up to ten years in prison and a fine of up to ten thousand dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: If no one is injured in a wreck but your car will not drive, whom do you call and what do you report?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.memory_hook: Call nine one one, report stuck
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: If nobody is hurt but your vehicle cannot be driven, call nine one one right away, give the location and say there are no injuries but you need police help.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: While waiting for help beside a vehicle that cannot be driven, what unsafe actions near the roadway must you avoid?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: While waiting with a vehicle that cannot move, be patient, keep away from traffic, and do not try to cross the road or stop cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: When nobody is hurt and your car still drives after a collision, where should you position it and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: If nobody is hurt and your vehicle can move, pull it off the road as near to the crash spot as you can to protect people and avoid backups.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How do the top prison and fine numbers compare between leaving a serious-injury crash and leaving a fatal crash?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Leaving a serious-injury crash risks up to five years and five thousand dollars, while leaving a fatal crash is a felony risking up to ten years and ten thousand dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Which seven pieces of personal, vehicle, and coverage information should every driver exchange after a crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Swap details with each other driver: name, address, phone, plate number and state, license number, vehicle make and model, and insurance.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What three contact details should you request from bystanders who saw the collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Ask any witnesses for their names, addresses and phone numbers.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Which four scene facts about where, when, vehicle count, and environment should you write down after a crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Note the crash location, date and time, number of vehicles, and weather and road conditions, and write them down if you can.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How should you document the harm to the cars and the sequence of the collision before leaving?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Record the vehicle damage in writing and photos if possible, and write down how the crash happened.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Where must you pull over right after striking an unattended car or other unattended property?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: If you hit an unattended vehicle or other unattended property, stop as near the spot as you can without blocking traffic more than needed.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: After hitting unattended property, what should you try first, and what must you leave if the owner cannot be found?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Then try to find the owner to explain and give your information, and if you cannot, leave a note with what happened and your contact details where it will be easily found.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What does Maryland law require you to do immediately if your car strikes and hurts a dog, cat, horse, or cow?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: If your vehicle hits and injures a domestic animal, such as a dog, cat, horse or cow, you must call the police right away.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Why should you get a broken-down vehicle onto the shoulder whenever possible instead of stopping in a lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: People are hurt or killed every year at the roadside while waiting for help, so move a disabled vehicle to the shoulder if you can.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Why is limping on a flat tire to an exit ramp or parking lot smart even if it ruins the wheel rim?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Reaching an off-ramp or parking lot is worth it even on a flat tire or at the cost of a rim, because more distance from traffic means more safety.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Which painted highway zone where an exit ramp branches off must you never use for stopping or parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Never stop or park in the painted triangular area where an exit ramp splits from the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: When remaining inside a broken-down vehicle is safe, how should you position yourself while waiting?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: If you can stay in the vehicle, keep your seat belt on and face forward so the vehicle's safety features protect you if you are hit.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: If staying inside a disabled car is too dangerous, how and where should everyone exit and shelter?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: If staying inside is unsafe, choose the safest moment to get everyone out, move quickly away from the road rather than standing by the car, and get behind an embankment, barrier or guardrail.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: After evacuating a disabled vehicle, what terrain should you seek and which direction should you face?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Once out of the vehicle, move to higher ground if you can, face oncoming traffic and stay alert for a car veering toward you.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Compare the right safety posture when you can stay inside a disabled vehicle versus when you must evacuate it?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: If you can stay in a disabled vehicle, stay buckled and face forward; if you cannot, get out at the safest moment and move away from the car behind a barrier.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Why do officers issue citations, and what do you risk if you ignore an officer's instructions during a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Officers write citations, or tickets, to people charged with breaking the Maryland Motor Vehicle Law, and if stopped you must follow the officer's directions or risk arrest.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: According to Maryland's safety campaign, what three human factors cause many pedestrian and bicyclist injuries and deaths?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: The campaign page notes that many pedestrian and cyclist injuries and deaths happen because drivers or pedestrians are drunk, do not know the laws, or are not paying attention.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: How often do motorcycle crashes injure the rider, and who causes over half of car-versus-motorcycle wrecks?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: Because riders lack a vehicle's protection, motorcyclists are injured in nearly seventy-five percent of crashes, and in car-motorcycle crashes the car driver is at fault more than half the time.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: What specific habit does the Look Twice safety message urge drivers to practice before merging, switching lanes, or pulling out?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: The Look Twice message asks drivers to check at least twice before merging, changing lanes or pulling into traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Where should you stop your car and which lights should you activate when police signal you over?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: When an officer stops you, pull to the side as far from traffic as you can and turn on your flashers.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: Once stopped by an officer, which two things should you turn off and what should you do with your window?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.memory_hook: Kill engine, mute radio, window down
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: During a stop, shut off the engine and radio and lower your window so you can talk with the officer.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What should you do with yourself and your seat belt while pulled over for a traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Remain in the vehicle with your seat belt fastened during a traffic stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: Where should your hands rest during a police stop, and what kind of cabin movements should you avoid?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Keep your hands where the officer can see them, ideally on the steering wheel, and avoid movements that could look like hiding or reaching for something.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Why shouldn't you debate a traffic ticket on the shoulder, and where is the proper place to contest it?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Do not argue about a citation at the roadside; you can make your case if you go to court.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Which vehicles on the roadway trigger Maryland's Move Over requirement when you approach from behind?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: Maryland's Move Over law requires you to move over when approaching any vehicle stopped, standing or parked on the road with its lights flashing.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: When changing lanes for a flashing roadside vehicle is impossible or unsafe, what must you do and how do you judge it?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: If moving over is unsafe or impossible, slow to a safe speed, judging it by weather, road conditions, traffic and pedestrians.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: What offense type, fine amount, and license point count come with a basic Move Over violation?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Breaking the Move Over law is a misdemeanor carrying a one hundred ten dollars fine and one point on your license.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: What fine and point penalty apply when failing to move over or slow down causes a collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: A Move Over violation that causes a crash carries a one hundred fifty dollars fine and three points.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What fine and license points result when a Move Over violation involves serious injury or death?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: A Move Over violation involving a death or serious injury carries a seven hundred fifty dollars fine and three points.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: How does the MVA use license points, and what can accumulating them ultimately cost you?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: The MVA tracks violations with points and uses them to issue penalties, and points can lead to suspension or revocation of your license.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Walk through all three Move Over fine and point tiers from a basic violation to a crash to serious harm or death?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: The basic Move Over penalty is one hundred ten dollars and one point, rising to one hundred fifty dollars and three points if a crash results and seven hundred fifty dollars and three points with a death or serious injury.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: At which three licensing moments must you notify the MVA if you have a listed medical condition?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: If you have a listed medical condition you must tell the MVA when you apply for or renew a license, or when the condition is diagnosed if that happens after licensing.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Which MVA unit or board must clear your license if a listed medical condition could impact your driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: For a listed condition that could affect driving, the MVA's Driver Wellness and Safety Division and or its Medical Advisory Board must approve you for a license.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What specific blood-sugar event and timeframe make diabetes reportable to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.memory_hook: Assisted low sugar within six months
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Diabetes is reportable when it caused a low blood sugar episode needing another person's help within the past six months.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: When must a driver report a heart condition to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: A heart condition is reportable when it caused a loss of consciousness within the past six months.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Falling short of what corrected visual acuity in one eye or what binocular field angle makes an eye issue reportable?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: An eye problem is reportable if it keeps your corrected acuity from reaching at least twenty over seventy in one eye or your binocular field of vision from reaching one hundred ten degrees.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Which five neurological, blackout, sleep, or brain-injury conditions appear on the MVA's reportable list?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Epilepsy or seizures, stroke, conditions causing dizzy spells, fainting or blackouts, sleep apnea or narcolepsy, and a history of traumatic brain injury are reportable.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: When must arm, hand, leg, or foot weakness, shaking, numbness, or an impaired or missing limb be reported?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Weakness, shaking or numbness in the arms, hands, legs or feet, or a missing, amputated or impaired limb, is reportable when it may affect your driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Which substance-use, mental health, and cognitive conditions must also be disclosed to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Alcohol or drug use problems, a mental health condition that may affect driving, schizophrenia and dementia are also reportable.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Which vehicles may a Maryland Learner's Permit holder operate, and who must always ride along?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: A Maryland Learner's Permit holder may drive only the vehicles or vehicle class the permit names, and always with a supervising driver.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What is the minimum age required to serve as a supervising driver for a permit holder?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: A supervising driver must be at least twenty-one years old.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How many years of licensing must a supervising driver hold, and do out-of-state licenses or vehicle class matter?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: A supervising driver must have held a license for at least three years, in Maryland or another state, for the same class of vehicle you are driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: Where inside the vehicle must your supervising driver sit, and which vehicle is the sole exception?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: The supervising driver must sit beside you, except when the vehicle is a motorcycle.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: Starting at what age may someone register as an organ donor on their own?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Anyone eighteen or older may become an organ donor.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: At what age may a minor register as an organ donor, and whose permission is required?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: A minor aged at least sixteen may be an organ donor with a parent's or guardian's written consent.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What can appear on your Maryland license if you opt into organ donation while applying or renewing?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: If you agree to be a donor on your application or renewal, your license can show that you are an organ donor.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Under the nineteen ninety-three federal Motor Voter law, what voting service must the MVA offer eligible license or ID applicants?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: The federal National Voter Registration Act of nineteen ninety-three, known as Motor Voter, requires the MVA to let eligible customers register to vote or update voter details when getting a license or photo ID card.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What licensing requirement applies to the insurance company covering any Maryland-registered vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Every vehicle registered in Maryland must be insured by a company licensed in Maryland.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: Which two kinds of liability coverage must Maryland vehicle owners carry, and where are the required minimums posted?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Vehicle owners must carry personal injury and property damage liability coverage in the amounts the law sets, which the MVA website lists.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: In what formats may you carry your valid insurance ID card while driving, and what happens if you cannot show an officer?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.memory_hook: Paper or digital proof avoids fines
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Always carry a valid insurance identification card when driving, which may be electronic, and show it when an officer asks or risk a fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: Who inside a motor vehicle must wear a seat belt or be strapped into a child safety seat under Maryland law?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: The law requires the driver and every passenger to wear a seat belt or be secured in a child safety seat.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: How do airbags protect best alongside your belts, and how many inches should separate your chest from the steering wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.memory_hook: Buckled, ten to twelve inches back
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Air bags protect best when used with the lap and shoulder belt and when you sit as far from the wheel as you can, keeping ten to twelve inches between the wheel and your chest.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How should a pregnant person position both the lap belt and the shoulder strap while riding or driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: A pregnant woman should wear the lap belt under the abdomen, low on the hips and across the upper thighs, with the shoulder belt over the rounding of the belly.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Compare the minimum age for a learner's supervising driver against the ages for independent and parental-consent organ donation?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: A supervising driver must be at least twenty-one, while organ donation is open at eighteen, or at sixteen with written parental consent.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Under what age must a child use a child safety seat, and what height lets a younger child transition out?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Every child under eight must ride in a child safety seat unless the child is at least four feet nine inches tall.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Until what age or seat limit must a young child ride rear-facing in a federally compliant car seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: A child younger than two must ride rear-facing in a seat meeting federal guidelines until reaching the maker's height or weight limit.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: Whose two sets of instructions govern child seat setup, and what devices count as child safety seats?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Follow every instruction from your child seat's maker and your vehicle's maker; child safety seats include car seats, booster seats and other federally approved devices.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Which Maryland Department of Health program offers low-cost car and booster seat rentals when families cannot afford one?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Families who cannot afford a seat can contact the Maryland Department of Health's Kids In Safety Seats program, which runs low-cost car and booster seat rentals, though seats are not always available everywhere.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Where must you never install a rear-facing infant or toddler car seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: A child in a rear-facing car seat must never ride in a front seat that has a passenger air bag.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Where should kids younger than thirteen ride, and how should they be restrained?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Children under thirteen should sit in the back, buckled into either a child safety seat or a seat belt.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What do anti-lock braking systems prevent during hard braking, and why does that matter?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Anti-lock braking systems keep the wheels from locking so you can keep control of the car.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: How does ABS react when a wheel starts locking, and what sound and pedal feel might surprise a driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: When the vehicle's computer senses a wheel locking, ABS pumps the brakes far faster than you could, and you may hear a rumble and feel the pedal vibrate.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: What is Maryland's rule on driving with earplugs, headsets, or earphones, and what device is permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: You may not drive wearing earplugs, headsets or earphones in both ears, but hearing aids are allowed.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: Up to how much in annual fines per vehicle can failing to carry required auto insurance bring in Maryland?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Driving without vehicle insurance is illegal, and failing to insure every vehicle brings fines of up to two thousand five hundred dollars per vehicle each year.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Line up the three age cutoffs for rear-facing seats, child safety seats, and riding in the back row?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: The rear-facing rule applies under age two, the child-seat rule under age eight unless four feet nine inches tall, and the rear-seat advice under age thirteen.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Where does parallel parking still show up in Maryland training, even though it was dropped from the road test?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Parallel parking is no longer part of the driving test, though it is taught in the MVA driver education course.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Which driving-course maneuver evaluates the exact same vision, space, mirror, signal, and pedal skills as parallel parking?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: The reverse two-point turn on the driving course test checks the same skills as parallel parking: vision, space judgment, mirrors and signals, steering, braking and acceleration control.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: Which three parking and turnaround maneuvers must you perform during the Maryland driving test?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: On the driving test you must complete pull-in parking, back-in parking and a three-point turn.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: What are the exact foot dimensions of the test parking stall and the three-point turn box?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: The test parking is done in a ten by twenty foot space and the three-point turn in a sixteen by twenty foot space.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Summarize which classic parking move is off the Maryland driving test versus which three maneuvers are required?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Parallel parking is not on the driving test, but pull-in parking, back-in parking and the three-point turn are required.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: How should bicyclists position themselves in a group, handle hazards and car doors, treat walkers, and follow traffic controls?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Cyclists should ride straight and single file, plan around hazards and opening car doors, yield to pedestrians and obey every signal and sign.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: On which side of the road must bicyclists travel, and how should they position themselves at intersections?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Cyclists must ride with traffic on the right side and use the correct intersection lane for left, straight or right.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: What two checks and signals should a bicyclist complete before shifting lanes or turning?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Cyclists should look back before changing lanes or turning and signal their turns.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: What are the two safe ways a bicyclist can complete a left turn at an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: A cyclist may turn left like a car from the left of the lane or a left turn lane, or stop, dismount and walk across in a crosswalk.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: How do rain or snow change bicycle braking, and which two road surfaces get especially slick?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Braking a bicycle in rain or snow needs extra stopping distance, and pavement markings and utility covers may be slippery.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.front: How must a bicycle carry a young child or small packages so the rider stays in full control?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.expected_back: A bicycle carrying a small child needs a firmly attached safety seat or trailer, and small items go in a basket, rack or bag so both hands stay on the bars.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: In the handbook's night-riding paragraph, what front light, rear reflector, and visibility distance does state law require?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.memory_hook: White front, red rear, six hundred
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: The night-riding paragraph says state law requires a white front headlight and a red rear reflector visible from at least six hundred feet.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: In the bicycle equipment list, from how many feet must the white headlight and red rear reflector each be visible?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.memory_hook: Five hundred front, six hundred rear
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: The equipment list says a bicycle ridden at night or in low light needs a white headlight seen from five hundred feet and a red rear reflector seen from six hundred feet.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.front: Who is legally required to wear a bicycle helmet in Maryland, including non-steering riders?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.expected_back: Anyone under sixteen on a bike must wear a helmet, passengers who are not steering included, and helmets are strongly advised for all ages.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.front: Within how many feet must legal bicycle brakes bring a bike to a stop from ten miles per hour on clean, dry, flat pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.expected_back: By law a bicycle's brakes must stop it within fifteen feet from ten miles per hour on dry, level, clean pavement.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.front: What pedal, wheel-count, and maximum motor-wattage rules define an electric bicycle in Maryland?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.expected_back: An electric bicycle runs on human power with motor help, has working pedals, two or three wheels and a motor rated at seven hundred fifty watts or less.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.front: When does a Class one electric bicycle provide motor help, and at what speed does that assist cut off?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.expected_back: A Class one electric bicycle assists only while you pedal and stops assisting at twenty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.front: How does a Class two electric bicycle deliver motor assistance, and at what speed does it stop helping?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.expected_back: A Class two electric bicycle assists whether or not you pedal and stops assisting at twenty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.front: How is motor help triggered on a Class three electric bicycle, and what is its cutoff speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.expected_back: A Class three electric bicycle assists only while you pedal and stops assisting at twenty-eight miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.front: What rider limit, weight cap, frame setup, and top powered speed define an electric low-speed vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.expected_back: An electric low-speed vehicle carries only its operator, weighs under one hundred pounds, has handlebars and a standing platform, and runs on motor and human power up to twenty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.front: Which two wheel layouts qualify as an electric low-speed vehicle, and what should riders verify locally?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.expected_back: Its wheels are either one in front and one behind in line, or one in front and two in back, and riders should check for local restrictions.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Contrast Class one, Class two, and Class three electric bicycles by pedaling requirement and cutoff speed?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.memory_hook: One-three pedal, two coasts, three fastest
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Class one and Class three electric bicycles both assist only while pedaling but cut out at twenty versus twenty-eight miles per hour, while Class two assists without pedaling and cuts out at twenty.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What credential do you need before operating any car, van, or pickup truck on Maryland roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: In Maryland you need a driver's license before you drive any motor vehicle, and cars, vans and pick-up trucks all count as motor vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: What does Maryland's vision screening measure, and which two providers are allowed to perform it?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the MVA or your own eye doctor may perform it.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Where should a Maryland applicant look for next steps after falling short of the standard vision numbers?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Applicants who do not meet the vision standards can find more information on the MVA website.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which section of the Maryland manual explains how to set up special accommodations for the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: If you need special accommodations for the knowledge test, the manual sends you to Section two.A for how to arrange them.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What online practice tool does the MVA provide, and what else must you study alongside it?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: The MVA website offers an Online Driver Test Tutorial with practice questions, and the manual says to study all of its contents as well.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: What does Maryland's driving skills test verify, and which two driving environments does it combine?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: The driving skills test is how the MVA confirms you can drive safely and responsibly, and it combines driving on public roads with a special course at the test site.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Can you walk in unscheduled for the Maryland driving skills test, or how must you set it up?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: The skills test requires an appointment, which you can book on the MVA website or by phone.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What three health and wellness guidelines does the MVA share for skills-test day inside the car?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.memory_hook: Fresh air, optional mask, reschedule sick
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: For health and safety during the test, the MVA encourages fresh air in the car, such as open windows, lets you wear a mask if you choose, and asks you to reschedule if you feel unwell.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What top fine or jail time can highway littering bring in Maryland, and how much trash do crews clear yearly?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Littering on Maryland roads can cost up to one thousand five hundred dollars or thirty days in prison, and highway crews pick up more than two million pounds of litter from state roads every year.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Compare where you may complete Maryland's vision screening versus where you must take the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The vision screening may be done by the MVA or by your own eye doctor, whereas the knowledge test is taken only at an MVA location.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which three screenings or tests must you pass to meet Maryland's core licensing requirements?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: The licensing requirements are three tests you must pass: a vision screening, a knowledge test and a driving skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How does a Maryland applicant find out whether additional safety requirements apply to their license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Some applicants must meet extra requirements to show they can drive safely, and the MVA tells you if that applies to you.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which three subject areas are evaluated on Maryland's driver knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: The knowledge test checks what you know about three areas: motor vehicle laws, safe driving practices and traffic signs.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Where do every single one of Maryland's knowledge-test questions come from, and where do you sit for it?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Everything the knowledge test covers is in the driver's manual, and you take the test at an MVA location.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What health disclosure does Maryland law require from drivers, and which manual section covers the details?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: State law requires you to tell the MVA about any medical condition that could affect your ability to drive, and Section ten lists which conditions to report and when.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does what the knowledge test measures differ from what the driving skills test evaluates?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The knowledge test covers laws, safe driving practices and signs, while the skills test checks actual driving on public roads and on a course at the test site.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does reporting a driving-related medical condition differ from MVA extra safety requirements in who speaks up first?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.memory_hook: You report medical; MVA flags extras
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Reporting a medical condition that could affect your driving is a legal duty you start yourself, unlike the extra requirements the MVA tells you about.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What does Maryland's binocular vision standard require your eyes to do?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: To qualify for a license you must have binocular vision, meaning both eyes working together.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: What minimum visual acuity score must you reach in each eye for a standard Maryland license?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The minimum visual acuity for a license is twenty over forty in each eye.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: At least how many degrees wide must your continuous field of vision be to qualify in Maryland?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: You also need a continuous field of vision of at least one hundred forty degrees.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What two rules apply if you rely on glasses or contact lenses to pass Maryland's vision screening?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will show that restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does Maryland's twenty-over-forty standard differ in what it measures from the one-hundred-forty-degree standard?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The acuity rule of twenty over forty is measured in each eye on its own, while the one hundred forty-degree rule is about how wide your continuous field of vision is, so they are two separate vision standards.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Name all three vision standards a standard Maryland license applicant must satisfy together?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: License qualification requires binocular vision alongside twenty-over-forty acuity per eye and a continuous one-hundred-forty-degree field of view.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Does needing prescription glasses or contacts block you from getting a Maryland license, and how is it handled?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Needing corrective lenses does not disqualify you; it means you must always wear them behind the wheel and your license states that condition.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Who supplies the car for Maryland's driving skills test, and what tag paperwork must it carry?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: You bring your own vehicle to the skills test, and it must carry current license plates and registration.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: What financial protection must you prove for the vehicle brought to your Maryland skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: You must be able to prove that the vehicle you use for the skills test is insured.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What mechanical and windshield standards must your skills-test car pass before going out?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: The test vehicle must be safe to drive and must have no windshield cracks or other objects that could block your view.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: How much fuel must be in the tank of the vehicle you bring to the Maryland skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: The test vehicle needs at least a half tank of gas.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Who must come with a learner to the skills-test site, and where are their qualifications listed?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: A supervising driver must accompany you to the test site, and Section ten of the manual explains who qualifies as one.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Who is allowed inside the cabin during the driving skills test, including the sole exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: During the skills test only you and the examiner may be in the vehicle, except that an MVA-approved interpreter may ride along if you need one.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: How does your supervising driver's role change once the examiner begins your behind-the-wheel test?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The supervising driver must come with you to the test site, but during the drive itself only you, the examiner and, if needed, an MVA-approved interpreter may be in the car.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Separate the skills-test vehicle checklist into its paperwork items versus its physical car conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Current plates and registration and proof of insurance are paperwork conditions on the test vehicle, while being safe, having a clear windshield and at least a half tank of gas are physical conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: What does visibility mean behind the wheel, and which four conditions most commonly cut it down?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Visibility means how clearly you can see vehicles, pedestrians, signs, signals and pavement markings, and darkness, fog, heavy rain and snow are its most common reducers.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: When fog, darkness, or storms make it hard to see ahead, what part of the roadway should guide your steering?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: When visibility is reduced, guide yourself by the road's edge lines or its right side.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Which side of your vehicle must yellow pavement markings stay on, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Yellow markings belong on your left, never your right, because yellow divides opposing traffic and marks the road's left edge.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Which two roadway boundaries or lane divisions do white pavement markings indicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: White markings show the road's right edge and also divide lanes moving in the same direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: What two safety jobs do your headlights perform when visibility drops?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Headlights both help you see in low visibility and help oncoming drivers see you.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Which three everyday conditions does the Maryland manual highlight as prime times to switch on your headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Night, fog and stormy weather are named as key times to use headlights.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What is traction, which three maneuvers depend on it, and how do wet roads change it?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Traction is the grip between tires and road that lets a vehicle start, stop and turn, and wet roads cut traction and raise crash risk.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Why must you drop speed in bad weather, and what tire upkeep standard should you maintain?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: In bad weather slow down to gain reaction time, and keep tire tread at the level the tire maker and your vehicle guidelines recommend.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Which abrupt steering and pedal habits must you avoid when driving in bad weather?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: In bad weather avoid jerking the wheel or changing speed suddenly.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Before heading into bad weather, what equipment should you check and what lights should you run?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: For bad weather, check that your windshield wipers work well and drive with your headlights on.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Which two vehicle reservoirs should you keep topped up throughout winter?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: In winter keep both the gas tank and the windshield washer fluid full.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: Which seven survival and traction supplies belong in your car's emergency kit?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A car emergency kit should hold flares, a flashlight with batteries, a first aid kit, a blanket, kitty litter or sand for traction, a small shovel and an ice scraper.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: Which five road-surface hazards—plus what driver choice—cut tire traction and invite skids?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Sand, gravel, rough pavement, oil, water and higher speed all reduce traction, which makes a skid or slide more likely.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: At what forward visibility distance does Maryland require you to switch on your headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: You must switch on your headlights whenever the light is too poor to see clearly at least one thousand feet ahead of your vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What does Maryland law require whenever inclement weather has your windshield wipers running?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Maryland law requires headlights on whenever you run your windshield wipers in inclement weather, meaning bad weather that may make driving unsafe.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: In which everyday night setting and three weather conditions should you run low-beam headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Use low beams in normal driving such as on a lit street at night, and in fog, rain or snow.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Why does Maryland advise turning on low beams when entering tunnels or construction zones even if not always mandated?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Low beams are also advised when entering a tunnel or a construction area; the law does not always demand it, but it helps other drivers and workers see you.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: What kind of roadways are high-beam headlights designed for, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: High beams are for roads with no streetlights, so you can see other vehicles and people.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: At least how many feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim high beams to low?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: You must dim to low beams at least five hundred feet before you meet an oncoming vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Within what distance behind a vehicle you are following must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: You must also dim to low beams when the vehicle you are following is three hundred feet or less ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Which two visual limitations make driving at night riskier than daytime driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Night driving is riskier because distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge and you can see only as far as your headlights reach.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Where should you aim your eyes—and where must you avoid staring—when bright oncoming headlights approach at night?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: At night, do not look straight into oncoming headlights; look at the road ahead or slightly right, toward the right edge of your lane or the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: How should you adjust your following gap at night, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: At night, leave more space behind the vehicle ahead so a sudden stop does not cause a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does Maryland's oncoming dimming distance compare with its following dimming distance?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: High beams must drop to low at least five hundred feet before an oncoming vehicle but at three hundred feet or less behind a vehicle you follow.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How should you adjust your speed in fog, especially once headlights or taillights appear ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: In fog, drive slower than normal, and slow even more when you see headlights or taillights ahead, ready to stop quickly.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: What two steps should you take when fog grows too dense to keep driving safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: If fog is too thick to drive safely, pull fully off the road to a safe spot and switch on your emergency flashers.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Which headlight setting—and optional lamps—should you use in fog?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: In fog use only low beam headlights, plus fog lights if your vehicle has them.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: How does the safe following gap change as pavement goes from dry to wet to snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: The gap you need behind the car ahead is much larger on wet roads than dry ones, and larger still on snow or ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Why must you avoid slamming the brakes, and how do you prevent skidding in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Slamming the brakes can start a skid; without an anti-lock braking system, pump the brakes to avoid skidding.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: Which roadway structures freeze before regular streets, and why can plowed roads still turn icy?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Ramps and bridges ice over before roads do, and plowed roads can refreeze at night or hold icy patches from daytime melt.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: What is black ice, and how does it form on asphalt?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Black ice is a thin, nearly invisible layer of ice on asphalt formed when ice or snow melts and freezes again.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Is there any guaranteed safe speed on snow and ice, and why do winter conditions shift from block to block?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: No speed is completely safe on snow and ice, and each road can differ with sun, shade and how much salt it has.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: Does driving a four-wheel-drive vehicle make you immune to sliding on snow and ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Four-wheel drive may give more control, but those vehicles can still slide on ice and snow.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: What must you brush and scrape completely clear before driving in snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Before driving in snow or ice, clear all ice and snow off the vehicle so its windows and lights are clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Which three gentle habits should you use when starting, checking grip, and approaching turns on snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: On snow or ice, start off very slowly, test your brakes gently, and begin slowing well before an intersection or turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: When Maryland declares a snow emergency, which three tire or traction options qualify on designated snow emergency routes?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: When a snow emergency is declared, use chains, snow tires or radial tires on designated snow emergency routes.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: The instant your vehicle starts skidding, what is your very first move with the pedals?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: In a skid, first ease off whichever pedal you are pressing, gas or brake, to regain control.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: Which direction do you steer and where do you look while recovering from a skid?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Steer in the direction of the skid and look where you want the vehicle to go.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: During a skid, when is it safe to touch the brake again, and what can help if rear wheels lose grip?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Brake only after your tires grip the road again, and gentle acceleration may help if the rear wheels lose traction.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: What physically happens between your tires and the pavement when your car hydroplanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Hydroplaning happens when speed and standing water rise until the tires ride on a sheet of water and lose contact with the road, costing some or all control.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: What two simple steps prevent hydroplaning before it starts?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: To prevent hydroplaning, keep tires in good shape and slow down on wet roads.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: What four-part response brings your car safely down if it starts hydroplaning?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: If you start hydroplaning, lift off the gas, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight and slow until control returns.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does the braking rule during hydroplaning differ from braking during a road skid?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: In a hydroplane you do not brake, while in a skid you may brake once the tires grip again.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: What basic fact about trains makes extra caution essential at every railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: Trains cannot stop quickly, so take extra care approaching and crossing railroad tracks.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.front: Which three types of vehicles must stop before every railroad crossing, even when no warning lights flash?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.expected_back: Buses, school buses and trucks hauling hazardous materials must stop before every railroad crossing, so expect them to stop ahead of you.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.front: What must you assume about train schedules, directions, and how close or fast a locomotive appears?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.expected_back: A train can come from either direction at any time and may be nearer and faster than it looks.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.front: What do flashing crossing lights or lowered gates mean, and when may you proceed?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.memory_hook: Stop until gates rise, lights off
sec07-card-sec07-F45.expected_back: Lowered gates or flashing warning lights mean the road is closed for now; stop and wait until the gates rise and the lights stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F46.front: Once the last railcar clears a crossing, why must you look both ways before moving?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.expected_back: After a train passes, look both ways and confirm the tracks are clear, since a second train may be on another track.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.front: What two clearance checks must be true before your front bumper enters railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.expected_back: Never start across tracks unless you can clear them fully before a train arrives and there is room for your vehicle on the far side.

sec07-card-sec07-F48.front: If an emergency strands your vehicle on or near railroad tracks, what do you do first and how do you report it?
sec07-card-sec07-F48.expected_back: In an emergency on or near a crossing, leave the vehicle and move away from the tracks, then report it using the blue and white Emergency Notification System sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F59.front: What defines a limited-access highway, and what makes an interstate a specific kind of one?
sec07-card-sec07-F59.expected_back: A limited access highway is a large road with no intersections or traffic lights and few entry and exit points; an interstate is one that runs between states.

sec07-card-sec07-F49.front: What activities create a work zone, and does a work zone always stay parked in one spot?
sec07-card-sec07-F49.expected_back: A work zone is a stretch of road where construction, maintenance or utility work is under way, and it may be stationary or move slowly along the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F50.front: Which five roadway changes should you anticipate inside a work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F50.expected_back: Work zones can bring new traffic patterns, narrow or shifted lanes, closed lanes and shoulders, pavement drop-offs and shorter sight distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F51.front: Which background color marks work-zone signage, and what mindset should it trigger?
sec07-card-sec07-F51.expected_back: Orange is the work-zone color, so orange signs mean pay close attention and expect unusual conditions ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F52.front: What do flashing amber or yellow lights inside a Maryland work zone tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F52.expected_back: Flashing amber or yellow lights in a work zone mean workers are present, so obey the signs, slow down and watch for them.

sec07-card-sec07-F53.front: What do flashing blue lights in a Maryland work zone indicate, and how do speeding fines behave there?
sec07-card-sec07-F53.expected_back: Work zones may use speed cameras, flashing blue lights show the cameras are active, and speeding fines can be much higher there, higher still with workers present.

sec07-card-sec07-F54.front: Which vehicles in or ahead of Maryland work zones may display flashing green lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F54.expected_back: Flashing green lights may appear on highway maintenance vehicles or service equipment in and ahead of work zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F55.front: Which six driving habits keep everyone safe while passing through an active work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F55.expected_back: In a work zone be ready to stop fully if traffic ahead stops, avoid distractions, merge carefully, do not tailgate, change lanes only if needed, and obey the flagger.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How do flashing amber, flashing blue, and flashing green lights differ inside Maryland work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.memory_hook: Amber workers, blue cameras, green crews
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Flashing amber or yellow in a work zone means workers present, flashing blue means speed cameras are active, and flashing green marks maintenance vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F56.front: What traffic control greets roads entering a traffic circle, and who always holds the right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F56.expected_back: Roads leading into a traffic circle have yield signs, and you must always yield to vehicles already in the circle.

sec07-card-sec07-F57.front: How do you approach a roundabout regarding speed, the center island, crosswalks, and an empty circle?
sec07-card-sec07-F57.expected_back: Approaching a roundabout, slow down, keep right of the island, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk, and wait at the yield line for a gap; with no traffic in it you need not wait.

sec07-card-sec07-F58.front: In a multi-lane traffic circle, how should you hold lanes and set up your exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F58.expected_back: In a multi-lane circle stay in your lane, and once you pass the exit before yours, signal right and move to the outside lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F60.front: How should you use an entrance ramp and acceleration lane, and what painted boundary must you not cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F60.expected_back: You reach a highway by an entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of highway traffic, and must not cross the solid lines between the entrance and the highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F61.front: Which lane must you use whenever possible if you are traveling slower than surrounding highway traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F61.expected_back: If you are slower than highway traffic, you must keep to the right lane whenever possible.

sec07-card-sec07-F62.front: When leaving a highway, when do you move right, where do you start braking, and what speed do you hit?
sec07-card-sec07-F62.expected_back: To exit, move right well before your exit, begin slowing in the deceleration lane, and slow to the exit ramp's posted limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F63.front: What must you do—and never do—if you accidentally take the wrong highway exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F63.expected_back: If you take the wrong exit, keep going off the ramp and find a way back; never stop and reverse anywhere on the highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F64.front: When is stopping on a highway shoulder permitted, and what two safety steps apply once parked there?
sec07-card-sec07-F64.expected_back: Stopping in moving highway lanes is not allowed; use the shoulder only for a breakdown or other emergency, turn on flashers and stay inside if you can.

sec07-card-sec07-F65.front: Which two light settings must vehicles in a Maryland funeral procession run, and what privilege does that grant at red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F65.expected_back: Drivers in a funeral procession must use headlights and flashing hazard lights, and with lights on they may go through a red signal.

sec07-card-sec07-F66.front: If your traffic light turns green while a lit funeral procession is crossing, what must you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F66.expected_back: Other drivers, even on a green signal, must yield to a funeral procession until it has all passed unless they can go without crossing its path.

sec07-card-sec07-F67.front: Which road users qualify as slow-moving vehicles, and what top speed does the rear emblem warn of?
sec07-card-sec07-F67.expected_back: Slow moving vehicles include bicycles, horse-drawn vehicles and farm vehicles, and a slow-moving sign on the back warns they go twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec07-card-sec07-F68.front: How should you drive behind a slow-moving vehicle, and what signal warns drivers approaching behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F68.expected_back: Near slow vehicles, adjust speed and position, pass only when safe, and use your emergency flashers while following one to warn drivers behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: What is the exact functional difference between an acceleration lane and a deceleration lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: An acceleration lane is for speeding up to join highway traffic, while a deceleration lane is for slowing down to leave it.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: How does Maryland view driving legally, and why might the MVA attach restrictions to your license?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and the MVA may place restrictions on your license to keep your driving safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Where do license restrictions come from, and what can happen if you drive in violation of one?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: A restriction limits your driving privileges and can come from your license type or from breaking motor vehicle laws; driving against a restriction is a serious offense that can cost you your privileges.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which four categories of restrictions apply to graduated license holders younger than eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Seat belt, passenger, nighttime and wireless device restrictions apply to graduated license holders under eighteen.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: When a Provisional License holder is behind the wheel, who inside the vehicle must be buckled or in a child seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: A Provisional License holder must always wear a seat belt, and every passenger must use a seat belt or child safety seat.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: May a permit or provisional driver use a hands-free phone while driving, and what is the sole exception?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Provisional License and Learner's Permit holders may not use any wireless communication device while driving, hands-free included, except to call nine one one in an emergency.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: For how many days is an unsupervised provisional driver under eighteen barred from carrying non-family passengers under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: A provisional driver under eighteen may not drive unsupervised with passengers under eighteen for the first one hundred fifty-one days, unless the passengers are immediate family.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: During that initial one hundred fifty-one day period, what makes it legal for an unrelated minor to ride along?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: During that period an unrelated passenger under eighteen may ride along only when a qualified supervising driver is also in the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Who qualifies as immediate family under Maryland's provisional teen passenger restriction?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Immediate family for the passenger rule means a spouse, child, stepchild, sibling or stepsibling, or any relative living at your address.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: During which overnight hours is unsupervised provisional driving restricted to specific approved trips?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Between twelve midnight and five a.m., unsupervised provisional driving is permitted only for qualifying work, organized volunteer, official school, or participating athletic travel.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Besides qualifying work, which three other activities allow unsupervised provisional driving between midnight and five in the morning?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: The other nighttime exceptions are trips to or from an organized volunteer program, an official school activity, or an athletic event or training session you take part in.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How does the one hundred fifty-one day passenger limit differ in duration and exceptions from the midnight-to-five rule?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: The passenger restriction is limited to the first one hundred fifty-one days, but the midnight to five a.m. rule allows unsupervised driving only for work, volunteer, school or athletic trips.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Simply by driving on Maryland roads or public-access private lots, what have you already agreed to do if asked by police?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: By driving or trying to drive on a road or on private property open to the public in Maryland, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test when an officer asks.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: When an officer suspects drug, alcohol, or controlled-substance impairment, which specialist may request a blood test?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: If an officer has reason to think you are impaired by drugs, alcohol or a controlled substance, a drug recognition expert may ask you to submit to a blood test.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What blood alcohol concentration on a chemical test triggers a license suspension?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Your license will be suspended if a test shows a blood alcohol concentration of point zero eight percent or more.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What action does the MVA take if you drive with impairing drugs in your system?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Drug impairment counts too: having drugs in your system that impair you leads the MVA to suspend your license.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: What happens once an officer submits written certification that you refused an alcohol or drug test?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Refusing a test also costs you: once an officer certifies in writing that you refused, the MVA suspends your license.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: What state and federal consequences can come from trying to get a fake ID, permit, or license?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Trying to obtain a fake identification card, permit or driver's license can bring fines, prison or both under federal and state law.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Even away from a car, what can lying about your age to buy, hold, or obtain alcohol do to your driver's license?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Lying about your age to buy, possess or get alcohol is illegal and, on top of other penalties, can lead to suspension of your license.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which four actions can the MVA take after violations, and what three facts appear in its mailed notice?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: For motor vehicle law violations the MVA may suspend, revoke, refuse or cancel a license, and it mails a notice giving the planned action, the reason and the steps to change or stop it.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: What can you usually request to present your side before a planned MVA license action takes effect?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: In most cases you may ask for an administrative hearing to explain why the action should not happen.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: What must you do with a suspended, revoked, refused, or canceled license, and when does the penalty timer actually start?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: If your license is suspended, revoked, refused or canceled you must surrender it to the MVA, and the suspension or revocation period starts when the MVA receives it.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: Who has the authority to ask the MVA to cancel the driver's license of someone under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: For a driver younger than eighteen, a parent or legal guardian may ask the MVA to cancel the license.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: What does a license suspension do, and what limited option might the MVA sometimes allow during it?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: A suspension takes away your driving privilege for a time, and in some cases the MVA may grant a restricted license for set purposes such as work and school trips.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: Why is revocation harsher than suspension, and when are you allowed to drive again after one?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Revocation is more serious than suspension: you may not drive until the MVA decides you can drive safely again.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: After a license revocation, what must happen before reinstatement, and is approval guaranteed?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: After a revocation you must wait a minimum period before asking the MVA to reinstate your license, and the MVA may say no.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: Which MVA license sanction is the most severe, and what does it do to your driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Cancellation is the most serious action: your driving privilege is ended and not restored.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: For what issuance or application problems may the MVA cancel a driver's license?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: The MVA may cancel a license that should never have been issued, or one obtained with missing or wrong application information or by fraud.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Contrast suspension, revocation, and cancellation in terms of how or whether your license comes back?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A suspension is temporary and may allow a restricted license, a revocation lasts until the MVA approves reinstatement, and a cancellation is never reinstated.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: What MVA sanctions can hit a Provisional License holder after a moving-violation conviction or Probation before Judgment?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: A conviction or Probation before Judgment for a moving violation while holding a Provisional License can mean a driver improvement program, a suspension or revocation, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: Once a provisional moving-violation suspension or revocation wraps up, what restriction follows on the license?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: When such a suspension or revocation ends, the license carries an employment and education only restriction.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: How do MVA provisional sanctions relate to any fines or penalties ordered by a court?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: These MVA penalties come on top of any court penalties for the conviction.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: How long is the fresh conviction-free period that restarts after every provisional moving conviction or PBJ?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: After each moving-violation conviction or PBJ you must start a new eighteen-month conviction-free period before you can get your license back.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: What sanction applies on a first moving conviction or PBJ for a provisional driver younger than eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: For a provisional driver under eighteen, a first moving-violation conviction or PBJ requires a driver improvement program.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What two-step sanction hits a provisional driver under eighteen upon a second moving offense?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: A second offense for a provisional driver under eighteen brings a thirty-day suspension and then a ninety-day employment and education only restriction.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Which three requirements apply when a provisional driver under eighteen racks up a third moving offense?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: A third offense for a provisional driver under eighteen brings a one hundred eighty-day suspension, a young-driver improvement program and a one hundred eighty-day employment and education only restriction.
