sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: What happens to a provisional driver under eighteen upon a fourth or later moving offense, including testing?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: A fourth or later offense for a provisional driver under eighteen means revocation, and every licensing test must be passed again to regain the license.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: For a provisional holder aged eighteen or older, what do a first offense and a second offense each bring?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: For a provisional driver eighteen or older, a first offense requires a driver improvement program and a second brings a thirty-day suspension.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: What penalty range faces a provisional driver eighteen or older on a third or subsequent offense?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: A third or later offense for a provisional driver eighteen or older brings up to a one hundred eighty-day suspension or a revocation.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How does a second provisional offense differ between drivers under eighteen and drivers eighteen or older?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Under eighteen, a second offense is a thirty-day suspension plus a ninety-day work-and-school restriction, while eighteen or older a second offense is a thirty-day suspension alone.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: At which offense number can revocation hit a provisional driver under eighteen versus one eighteen or older?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Revocation comes at a fourth offense for a provisional driver under eighteen, but a third offense can already bring revocation for one who is eighteen or older.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: What consequence can come from misusing disability parking spaces, license plates, or placards?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.memory_hook: Misusing disability parking brings big fines
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: Misusing disability parking spaces, plates or placards can bring big fines.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What two conditions must both be met before a vehicle may legally park in a disability space?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: You may park in a disability space only with an MVA-issued disability plate or placard and with the qualifying person in the vehicle as driver or passenger.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: May a vehicle displaying a valid disability plate or placard park in front of or block part of a curb cut?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: Parking in front of or blocking any part of a curb cut is a violation even if you hold a disability plate or placard.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: Why is parking on any part of the striped access aisle beside a disability stall illegal even with a placard?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: Parking on any part of the access aisle beside a disability space is a violation even with a plate or placard; the aisle is the space wheelchair and mobility-device users need to get in and out.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: Which three credential or presence mistakes turn using a disability plate or placard into a violation?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: Using an expired placard, or a plate or placard without the disabled person present and proper identification, is a violation.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: How does Maryland treat fraud or misrepresentation when applying for a disability plate or placard?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: Any fraud or misrepresentation in applying for a disability plate or placard is also a violation.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.front: What device must a driver caught drinking and driving install, and how does it work?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.expected_back: A driver caught drinking and driving will have to install a breathalyzer car lock that keeps the vehicle from starting when alcohol is detected.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What three items make up traffic control devices, what do they do, and why must everyone obey them?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Traffic control devices are the signals, signs and pavement markings that regulate, warn and guide traffic, everyone must obey them, and ignoring them is a major cause of crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Which specific people on duty can legally direct you to disobey a posted traffic control device?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: You may depart from a traffic control device only when a police officer or other emergency personnel, or a uniformed school crossing guard directing traffic near a school, tells you to.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Are you allowed to cut across a corner lot or leave the roadway to bypass a traffic control device?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: You may not cut across private property or leave the road at an intersection to get around a traffic control device.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Where exact three places, in order of priority, must you stop when a traffic light goes completely out?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: When a traffic signal is not working, stop at the clearly marked stop line, which is a wide white line painted across the road; with no stop line, stop before the crosswalk; with neither, stop before entering the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: After stopping at a non-working traffic light, whom do you yield to and when may you proceed?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: At a dark signal, yield to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection and stay stopped until you can safely enter and go through.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does lawful direction past a traffic light differ from cutting across private property at a corner?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A police officer, emergency worker or uniformed school crossing guard can direct you contrary to a signal, but no one may avoid a signal by cutting through private property.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How does waiting at a dark, non-working traffic light compare with waiting at a steady red light?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: A dark, non-working signal and a steady red both require a stop at the stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge, but at a dark signal you stay stopped only until it is safe to enter and continue through.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Where must you halt at a steady red light, and how long must you remain there if going straight?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: At a steady red signal, stop completely at the stop line, or before the crosswalk and intersection if there is none, and stay stopped while the light is red.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: When no sign forbids turning, which two turns are legal after a complete stop at a red light?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop at a red signal you may turn right, or turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Who holds the right-of-way over your vehicle whenever you make a legal turn during a red phase?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: When you turn on red, you must yield to pedestrians and to all other traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What transition does a steady yellow light warn about, and what should you do based on your distance?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: A steady yellow signal means the light is changing from green to red, giving you time to stop safely and letting vehicles already in the intersection clear it; if you are too close to stop safely, continue through carefully.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Before moving forward or turning on a steady green light, what must you check and yield to first?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: On a steady green signal, first check that no vehicles are in the intersection, then go straight or turn with caution unless a sign or signal prohibits the turn, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already there.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Assuming no prohibiting sign stands at the corner, how do right-on-red rules differ from left-on-red rules?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless a sign forbids it, but left on red is allowed only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Once you come to a full stop, how does your next move differ between steady red and flashing red?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: A steady red requires you to stay stopped for as long as it is red, whereas after stopping at a flashing red you may go once the way is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What separates the moment you must brake on steady yellow from the moment you keep moving through?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A steady yellow means stop safely if you can because red is coming, while you continue carefully only when you are too close to stop safely.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: What must you do when facing a steady red arrow pointing in the direction you plan to travel?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: A steady red arrow means that if you want to go the way it points, you stop completely before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection and stay stopped while the arrow is red.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What is ending when a steady yellow arrow illuminates, and how should you adjust your driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow means permission to turn that way is ending, so slow down and proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Even when a steady green arrow grants movement in its direction, whom must you still yield to?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: A steady green arrow lets you go with caution in the direction it points, but you must still yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: What separates the message of a steady yellow arrow from the message of a flashing yellow light?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow signals that turn permission is ending, while a flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How does a steady red arrow differ from a flashing red arrow after you stop at the line?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: A steady red arrow keeps you stopped while it is red, but a flashing red arrow lets you go in its direction after a full stop once traffic and pedestrians are clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What three steps must you complete when approaching a standard intersection with a flashing red light?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: At a flashing red signal, stop completely at the stop line, or before the crosswalk and intersection, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and go when the way is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: When red lights flash at railroad tracks and you cannot see a train anywhere, what must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: At a railroad crossing with a flashing red signal, stop completely even if no train is visible, and go only after the flashing stops and the way is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: How must you adjust your driving when you approach a flashing yellow traffic light?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What sequence of actions is required before moving in the direction of a flashing red arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: A flashing red arrow means stop completely before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go in the arrow's direction when clear.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Why does a flashing red light at railroad tracks break the usual stop-and-go rule of intersection flashers?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: A flashing red at a railroad crossing is the exception: you stay stopped until the light stops flashing and the way is clear, even when no train is in sight.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: How do reversible lanes work throughout the day, and what tells you which direction is open?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Reversible lanes carry traffic one way at some hours and the other way at other hours depending on traffic volume, and lane use signals, signs and markings show which way you may go.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: Between an overhead red X and an overhead green arrow, which lane may you use and which is off-limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Never drive in a lane under a red X signal, but you may drive in a lane under a green arrow signal.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What action must you take right away if a steady yellow X illuminates above your travel lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: A steady yellow X over a lane means leave that lane as soon as you safely can.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What lane use is permitted underneath a flashing yellow X or two-way left-turn arrows?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A flashing yellow X or two-way left-turn arrows mean the lane is for left turns, and you will probably share it with left-turning drivers coming the other way.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: How does a walker trigger a roadside crosswalk beacon, and which road users get signaled first?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: A crosswalk signal halts traffic so pedestrians can cross safely; a pedestrian activates it with a push button on a roadside pole, and it signals drivers to stop before telling pedestrians to cross.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What does each of the four crosswalk beacon phases—flashing yellow, solid yellow, solid red, and flashing red—tell a driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: For drivers at a crosswalk signal, flashing yellow means slow down, solid yellow means get ready to stop, solid red means stop, and flashing red means stop and then proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: How does your required action under a steady yellow X compare with driving under a flashing yellow X?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Over a lane, a steady yellow X means get out of the lane, while a flashing yellow X means the lane is shared for left turns.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which two documents must you carry and what three cabin checks come before driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Setting your seat, mirrors, belts, and glovebox paperwork while parked keeps your focus outside once rolling.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What fundamental rule governs vehicle control every moment you are behind the wheel, and why?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Safe operation rests legally on the driver, leaving no excuse when distractions or speed cause a loss of control.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Where does a defensive driver keep looking, and what two adjustments does early scanning prepare for?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Sweeping ahead, beside, and in mirrors spots closing hazards early enough for calm speed or lane changes.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What six habits help manage roadway risk, including what you must never assume about other motorists?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Expecting another driver to obey every stop sign or blinker leaves you exposed the instant they slip up.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: What does yielding the right-of-way mean in practice, and what mindset trap must you avoid?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Right-of-way is something one user gives another to prevent crashes, never an automatic pass to force ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Who yields when one vehicle reaches an intersection later versus when two vehicles arrive together?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Letting the car to your right break simultaneous ties prevents awkward double-starts in the middle.
sec03-card-sec03-F06.must_match_memory_hook: First arrives goes; ties yield right

visual_sync.text_span: First arrives goes; ties yield right

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: At a four-way stop, which tie-breaker applies and which three road users inside the intersection get priority?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Anyone walking, biking, or driving still inside the box holds priority before stopped cars launch.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Whom must you yield to when stopped on the stem of a T intersection or facing a yield sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Vehicles on the continuing through road carry full speed with no stop sign holding them back.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: When making a left turn, which stream of traffic holds priority over your turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Cutting across oncoming headlights misjudges closing speed and triggers severe front-corner collisions.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you pull out of a driveway or merge off a highway acceleration ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Main-road and highway vehicles already hold established lane speed, so newcomers must match and yield.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: When does the yield-to-the-right rule decide intersection order versus first-to-arrive?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Applying the right-side rule when another car clearly stopped earlier steals their rightful turn.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Contrast which traffic stream you yield to during a left turn versus pulling from a driveway or ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Left turns cross oncoming lanes head-on, whereas driveways and ramps join all established road traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What conditions does a posted speed sign assume, and whose job is choosing a safe pace?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Rain, darkness, or glare can make the legal dry-pavement maximum unsafe long before reaching the number.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Up to the posted limit, what speed is safest in normal flow, and why is creeping much slower risky?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Crawling well under normal flow forces stream after stream of passes behind you and raises crash odds.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What five control, perception, and impact problems make speeding one of the top crash causes?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Speed shrinks curve grip and reaction time while fooling cross-street drivers about how fast you close.
sec03-card-sec03-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Weaker control, longer stops, harder hits

visual_sync.text_span: Weaker control, longer stops, harder hits

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Under Maryland Vehicle Law, when may you drive below a posted speed limit, and may you ever drive above it?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Adjusting downward for hazards obeys Maryland's reasonable-speed rule, whereas exceeding the sign is always illegal.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: For what kinds of road geometry, slick surfaces, busy zones, structures, or crossings does Maryland advise slowing?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Tight bends, wet asphalt, shopping lots, schools, narrow bridges, toll plazas, and rail tracks all compress reaction space.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Compare the legality of slowing below the limit in bad conditions versus speeding to match fast traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Telling an officer everyone else was going eighty never legalizes driving past the posted number.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: How do train tracks meet the roadway at a railroad grade crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Without an overpass or tunnel separating rails from asphalt, trains and cars share the exact same crossing surface.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Which four human, surface, and mechanical factors control how far your car travels while stopping?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Slow hazard recognition or worn tires on wet asphalt stretch your stop long after touching the pedal.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Where should you choose to park, and how should your tires sit relative to traffic and any curb?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Tucking tight against the curb inside designated stalls keeps mirrors and fenders clear of passing lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: What four steps secure your vehicle and protect passing traffic before you walk away from a parked car?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Setting brake and transmission stops rollaways while checking mirrors before opening doors protects cyclists.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What causes most rear-end collisions, and how many seconds of following space does the MVA advise?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Tailgating steals reaction time, so Maryland sets a three-to-four-second cushion even on dry clear days.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How do you use a roadside landmark and counting phrase to verify at least a three-second gap?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Timing against a sign, bridge, or milepost adjusts your physical gap automatically as highway speed rises.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: To how many seconds should you widen your following gap behind transit buses or delivery vans?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Wide box vans and buses hide brake lights ahead and halt repeatedly at curbs, tracks, and stops.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: How does Maryland's standard dry-road following gap step up when trailing frequent-stopping buses or vans?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Adding at least one extra second behind frequent stoppers prevents surprise rear-end brake slams.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Contrast how following distance is measured against the four factors that determine stopping distance?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Counting seconds manages your live buffer, whereas perception, pavement, tread, and brakes govern hard stops.
sec03-card-sec03-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Seconds count gap; four factors stop

visual_sync.text_span: Seconds count gap; four factors stop

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: How should you hold your lane, and where is changing lanes specifically off-limits?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Swapping lanes mid-intersection surprises turning cross-street drivers who expected your original lane to stay put.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which three situations allow driving left of the roadway center in Maryland?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Every other moment belongs right of center so opposing traffic keeps an unblocked path.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: What five habits prepare you cleanly before executing any street turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Checking signs, signaling early, scanning all four sides, and scrubbing speed beforehand keeps turns smooth.
sec03-card-sec03-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Check signs, plan, signal, scan, slow

visual_sync.text_span: Check signs, plan, signal, scan, slow

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Where U-turns are permitted in Maryland, how do you signal, yield, and choose your finishing lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Swinging into the outside right-hand lane handles a wide turning radius cleanly once oncoming lanes clear.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: Along stretches posted with Stay Right signs, when is leaving the right-hand lane allowed?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Keeping through vehicles right opens the left lane cleanly for overtaking and emergency response.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Which blinker starts a legal Maryland U-turn, and why watch which opposite lane you finish in?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Test takers often guess the inside center lane, yet Maryland specifies finishing in the outside right-hand lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What steps come before passing, and what exact mirror sight confirms it is safe to merge back?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Waiting until both headlamps show in your inside mirror guarantees you will not clip their front bumper.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Which side is standard for passing, and under what conditions is passing on the right legal?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Right-side passes stay legal only on paved lanes past a left-turner or on multi-lane roads your way.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: What two obligations fall on you whenever another motorist is overtaking your vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Racing a passing car traps them exposed beside you and multiplies head-on collision risk.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Contrast the duty of the driver being passed with the duty of the overtaking driver?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Teamwork keeps passing safe when one driver holds steady speed and the other clears both headlights first.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Even when a car ahead is waiting to turn left, may you ever leave the road onto the shoulder to pass?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Every legal right-side pass requires open roadway width and never excuses cutting onto gravel or paved shoulders.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Which four zone, center-line, or traffic conditions bar you from overtaking?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Solid yellow on your side, double yellow stripes, or crowding oncoming traffic leaves zero safe passing margin.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: Where do hilltops, curves, bridges, elevated roads, and tunnels make passing illegal?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Pulling out blind near crests, bends, or within a hundred feet of sight-blocked structures invites head-on hits.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: Within what distance of intersections or railroad grade crossings is passing banned, alongside shoulders?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Turning cars, cross traffic, and trains make overtaking inside that hundred-foot approach buffer deadly.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How does Maryland's hundred-foot no-passing rule at intersections and tracks differ from bridges and tunnels?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Intersections and rails ban passing within a hundred feet unconditionally, whereas bridges and tunnels add blocked view.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: How does a single solid yellow center line differ from double solid yellow lines for passing?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: A broken stripe paired beside solid yellow lets only the broken side pass, while double solids lock both.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: What three visual features let a driver recognize any road message quickly at highway speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Glare, snow, or distance can blur small lettering, so recognizing outline and hue gives you extra braking time.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What quick clue do you get just from spotting a panel's main background color down the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Spotting orange or red blocks ahead lets your brain prep for work crews or stops long before text becomes readable.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What four urgent commands or warnings does a red background communicate to drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Red always flags life-or-death conflict points where ignoring a restriction sends you into cross traffic or wrong-way lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What broad category of information does a standard yellow background deliver to approaching drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Treating yellow panels as casual scenery instead of easing off the throttle leaves you too fast for curves or merges.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: What specific roadside environment is announced whenever you spot an orange background?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Construction crews, shifted lanes, and sudden slowdowns sit just ahead, where distracted speeding triggers severe penalties and crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Which three vulnerable road-user groups are protected by fluorescent yellow-green panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Bright neon cuts through dawn, dusk, and rain where kids, walkers, and cyclists cross unexpectedly near traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Alongside turn bans and Left Turn Only, which five classic restriction messages appear in the manual's regulatory set?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Missing a white-and-red restriction panel at an unfamiliar junction leads straight into wrong-way lanes, illegal passing, or tow zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: What four lane, median, left-turn, and parking rules appear among the manual's additional regulatory examples?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Drivers often forget that lane reservations, left-turn green yields, and disability parking rules carry full legal force just like speed limits.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How do standard yellow, orange, and fluorescent yellow-green divide up warning duties on the road?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Permit questions love scrambling those three bright shades to check whether you separate roadwork from school and pedestrian zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Which three types of roadway rules or guidance appear on white backgrounds?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: White backgrounds usually post enforceable traffic rules, so ignoring a white panel risks an immediate moving violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What three pieces of navigation help do green highway boards give drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Reading green exit and mileage boards early stops last-second multi-lane swerves across highway gore areas.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What roadside needs are pointed out by blue highway panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Spotting blue exit boards lets tired or low-fuel drivers pull off cleanly instead of stopping on dangerous highway shoulders.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: What two kinds of destinations are marked by brown roadside panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Knowing brown flags parks and historic sites helps you anticipate tourists slowing down or turning near trailheads.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What sudden roadside situation is marked with fluorescent pink panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Spotting bright coral-pink warns you of active crashes or responder blockades ahead that differed from planned orange roadwork.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Which two kinds of roadway displays use a black background?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: High-contrast black makes directional arrows and electronic overhead alerts pop clearly against bright daytime sky or headlights.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How do green, blue, and brown highway boards split up navigation information for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Test questions regularly pair green, blue, and brown together to verify you never confuse rest-stop services with park entrances.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What geometry has eight sides on the road, and what exact vehicle action does it always demand?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Even if mud, snow, or vandalism hides the front, spotting eight sides from behind or afar still requires halting your wheels.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What command does a downward-pointing triangle give, and how must you handle crossing traffic and walkers?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Breezing past a triangle without slowing down leaves zero margin to stop when cross traffic or walkers claim the lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What lies ahead when you spot a diamond outline, and how should you prepare to respond?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Diamond alerts give you advance seconds to cover the brake before curves, merges, or slick pavement catch you off guard.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: What zone starts where a pennant-shaped panel stands, and what maneuver is banned there?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side of two-lane roads, the pennant remains visible even when a tall truck blocks right-shoulder posts.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: What two child-safety locations are marked by a five-sided pentagon outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Mistaking a roof-shaped pentagon for a diamond hazard misses the strict speed and crosswalk vigilance needed around children.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What specific hazard up ahead is announced exclusively by a round roadside outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Trains cannot swerve and take huge distances to stop, so circular advance warnings tell you to quiet down, look, and listen early.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Where does a white X-shaped crossbuck stand, and what exact spot does it pinpoint?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Unlike the round yellow advance warning back up the road, the crossbuck stands right at the grade crossing where tracks cross asphalt.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which road command owns the sole eight-sided outline on the highway, and what are its letter and background colors?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Giving stop its own exclusive eight-sided silhouette guarantees drivers recognize cross-street priority from front or back in blizzards.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Which road command owns the sole three-sided outline, and how are its letters and background colored?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Keeping the three-sided outline exclusive to yield lets drivers spot merge duties instantly from any angle.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How do stop and yield panels contrast in both their exclusive side counts and their color schemes?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Reversing red-and-white letter pairings is a favorite multiple-choice distractor on state learner permit exams.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does the braking requirement for an octagon differ from the braking requirement for a triangle?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Rolling an octagon like a clear yield draws an instant failure on road tests, whereas unnecessary dead stops on clear merges risk rear-enders.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How does a circular railroad panel differ in placement and role from a crossbuck?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Confusing advance warning with the physical track marker leaves fast rural drivers braking way too late for an approaching locomotive.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What separates the meaning of a diamond, a pennant, and a five-sided pentagon?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Permit tests routinely bundle four-sided, three-pointed pennant, and five-sided silhouettes together to check rapid hazard recognition.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: How does the usual message of a vertical rectangle differ from that of a horizontal rectangle?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Vertical boards carry enforceable laws like speed or parking caps, whereas wide boards orient you toward exits and routes.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: What three recreational or route destinations are marked by a trapezoid outline?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Spotting a slanted trapezoid cues you into park entrances, historic areas, and forest roads where visitors brake unexpectedly.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: What do regulatory panels state, and are drivers legally required to follow them?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Treating a regulatory board like a friendly suggestion invites tickets, license points, and right-of-way crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What color and geometry regulate traffic speeds, and what exact limit does a speed limit board set?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Posted numbers cap your top speed under ideal conditions rather than promising a safe speed in rain, fog, or heavy traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: When comparing two rectangular road boards, what tells you one states a rule while the other gives directions?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Flipping tall and wide rectangles is an easy exam trap when test makers ask about shape-only outlines without text.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Where exact three places, in fallback order, must you halt your wheels at a posted stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Stopping past the white bar or across pedestrian stripes forces walkers into live lanes and fails road-test scoring.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Once you make a full stop at a stop post, whom must you yield to and how long must you wait?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Tapping the brakes and immediately pulling out ignores cross traffic that has no stop requirement at two-way intersections.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: What step-by-step routine must you follow as you roll toward a yield post?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Checking both left and right for bikes, walkers, and cars prevents merge collisions when entering roundabouts or channelized turns.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What maneuver does a Two-way Left panel authorize for traffic flowing from both directions?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Cruising straight down a shared center turn lane to pass queues sets up a head-on wreck with opposing left turners.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What restriction does a One Way panel place on every lane of that roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Turning against a One Way arrow puts you bumper-to-bumper with oncoming multi-lane traffic that never expects head-on cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: What requirement must your car meet before you enter a High Occupancy Vehicle lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Solo drivers who slip into restricted carpool lanes face steep enforcement fines and disrupt express transit flow.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How does traffic movement under a Two-way Left panel contrast with movement under a One Way panel?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Confusing bidirectional center-turn arrows with one-way street arrows causes wrong-way turns at divided urban corridors.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Why do highway engineers place warning panels upstream of certain road features?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Hills, trees, and blind curves hide stopped queues or sharp bends until you are inside braking distance at cruising speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: Which three advance warning panels alert you that a mandatory traffic control sits just around the bend?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Spotting an advance control warning lets you start smooth braking before cresting a hill onto backed-up red-light traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: Which five specific construction-zone warnings are highlighted in the manual's work-area section?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Recognizing work-zone start, flagger, detour, and end markers tells you exactly where crew hazards and work-zone rules apply.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: What penalty warning accompanies the manual's work-zone panel that activates when its beacons flash?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Active flashing lights mean road workers are exposed steps from live bumpers, triggering heavier citations for violations.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: What five alignment or grade changes do road-shape warning panels preview for drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Shedding speed before entering a sharp bend or steep downgrade keeps tires gripping asphalt and brakes from overheating.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: What four lane-drop, merge, or median transitions do lane-change warning panels announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Early notice that your lane ends or a median stops prevents last-second side-swipes and head-on drift into two-way traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: Which four junction layouts—including roundabouts and rail-adjacent corners—appear in the manual's intersection warning set?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Knowing railroad tracks sit right before a T-junction stops you from queuing across the rails while waiting to turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: Which five groups of people, vehicles, or animals are covered by the manual's crossing warning panels?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Scanning roadsides at deer, trail, and heavy-truck crossings gives you crucial braking margin when something darts or pulls out.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: Alongside alignment and crossing alerts, which traction warning and passing restriction appear in the manual's warning set?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Rain lifts oil film onto smooth pavement fast, making sudden braking or passing attempts spin out of control.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Which two advance alerts warn drivers about students walking or boarding ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Hidden school bus stops beyond hills or curves demand immediate speed drops before flashing red bus arms appear.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: Where are overhead lane-use boards mounted, and what three things do they tell drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Picking the right highway lane early from overhead gantries eliminates dangerous last-second weaves across multi-lane interchanges.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: What two pieces of highway identity are displayed together on a route marker shield?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Matching both the shield outline and route digits keeps you from turning onto a state highway that shares numbers with a United States route.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: How do service information and guide boards help travelers choose highway exits?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Knowing which exit offers fuel or medical care prevents drivers from reversing on ramps or hunting distractedly at high speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.question_text: Which seven traveler facilities and transit hubs appear among the manual's service and guide examples?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.teaching_text: Recognizing hospital, airport, rail, and park-and-ride symbols instantly lets you navigate emergencies or commuter transfers without reading fine print.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.question_text: At what exact interval are mile marker posts placed along interstate highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.teaching_text: Consistent one-mile spacing lets you track progress between exits and pinpoint breakdowns on long rural stretches.

sec05-card-sec05-F49.question_text: Why should you note the nearest mile marker number if a crash or breakdown strands you on the highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F49.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers an exact mile number gets tow trucks, paramedics, or troopers to your shoulder fast when no cross streets exist.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What letter class designates Maryland's noncommercial license for ordinary cars, vans, and pickup trucks?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Knowing Class C stands for standard noncommercial passenger vehicles keeps commercial weight classes separate on exam day.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: How do you begin a Maryland license application at the MVA, and what age-and-name document do you bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Branch visits start by appointment, and your age proof must display your complete legal name.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Alongside lawful-status and Social Security proof, how many Maryland residency documents must you bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Showing up with only one piece of mail sends you home empty-handed when two Maryland residency proofs are required.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Which document versions does the MVA accept, and which three kinds get turned away?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Bringing plain photocopies, notarized sheets, or papers with erasures causes an automatic counter rejection.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Which education course must every Maryland permit holder younger than twenty-five finish, and who must teach it?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Taking unapproved online courses will not count toward provisional eligibility because only MVA-approved schools qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: In what official record does every permit holder track supervised driving time, and where can you download a copy?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Keeping your Practice and Skills Log updated drive-by-drive prevents last-minute guesswork before your road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Which permit type is built for someone never previously licensed, how long does it last, and what tests unlock it?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Passing vision and written rules opens up two full years of supervised practice on a Type one permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Who uses a Type two learner's permit, and what minimum age, validity cap, and wait period apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Drivers already holding a license only wait fourteen days within a six-month window when upgrading classes.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What personal factor sets your permit holding period before a Provisional License, and what term names a permit seeker?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Maryland's graduated system scales minimum permit wait times directly by the applicant's age bracket.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Contrast who needs a Type one permit versus a Type two permit and how long each stays valid?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Mixing up brand-new drivers' two-year window with class-upgraders' one-hundred-eighty-day cap is a classic written-test trap.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How old must a Maryland applicant under twenty-five be to apply for a learner's permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Maryland sets the entry line three months shy of sixteen rather than right on your sixteenth birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How many total and nighttime supervised hours must an applicant under twenty-five log, and how is night defined?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Twilight glare and dark headlights challenge beginners most, so ten logged hours must fall inside that specific dusk-to-dawn window.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: What driver-ed and supervised-hour totals, including night hours, apply to a permit holder aged twenty-five or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Adult learners twenty-five and up still take approved driver ed while logging a shorter fourteen-hour, three-night track.
sec02-card-sec02-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Driver ed, fourteen total, three night

visual_sync.text_span: Driver ed, fourteen total, three night

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: At least how many days must an applicant aged twenty-five or older hold their learner's permit before Provisional?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Older beginners get a forty-five-day minimum hold instead of the multi-month waits placed on younger drivers.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How does the minimum age for a first-time permit under twenty-five compare with the Type two permit minimum?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Because Type two requires already holding a license, its floor sits nine months older at sixteen and six months.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: Compare total and nighttime supervised practice hours for learners under twenty-five against learners twenty-five and up?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Pairing sixty-and-ten against fourteen-and-three keeps both Maryland practice-log brackets ready for instant recall.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Alongside a parent or guardian co-signer under eighteen, what extra school form must an applicant under sixteen submit?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Fifteen-year-old applicants must verify school attendance with a completed DL-300 certification at the MVA counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Who counts as a minor in Maryland licensing, who normally co-signs, and what documents prove that relationship?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Staff verify relationship legal standing through an original or certified birth certificate or court guardianship order.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: When may an adult spouse or a responsible adult like an employer co-sign a minor's license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Marriage papers clear an eighteen-plus spouse, while death or emancipation proof unlocks an employer co-signer.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: How can a co-signer revoke a minor's Maryland license, and how long does that cancellation stay in place?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Filing with Administrative Adjudication suspends driving until age eighteen unless a qualified adult signs a fresh application.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: In what priority order does Maryland allow parents, spouses, or responsible adults like employers to co-sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: An employer or other responsible adult cannot step in while a parent, legal guardian, or adult spouse exists.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: At any age, what happens to your permit wait after a moving-violation conviction, PBJ, or any suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Even Probation Before Judgment restarts a full nine-month holding clock regardless of whether you are sixteen or forty.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: How many violation-free months must a permit holder younger than eighteen complete before Provisional?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Starting at fifteen and nine months pairs naturally with nine clean months to hit sixteen and six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: How long must an eighteen-year-old graduate or someone aged nineteen to twenty-four hold a clean permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Finishing high school or GED at eighteen, or turning nineteen, cuts the clean permit hold from nine months to three.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Line up Maryland's three clean-permit holding periods across under-eighteen, nineteen-to-twenty-four, and twenty-five-plus?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Seeing nine months, three months, and forty-five days side by side keeps every age bracket unmistakable.
sec02-card-sec02-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Nine months, three months, forty-five days

visual_sync.text_span: Nine months, three months, forty-five days

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How does the nine-month violation or suspension clock interact with shorter adult permit minimums?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: A thirty-year-old who normally waits forty-five days still faces nine full months after a ticket, PBJ, or suspension.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Who enters the Provisional License stage, and what mix of solo freedom and limits comes with it?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Graduating past a mentor lets you drive alone while curbing high-risk teen passengers and late-night hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: At least how long must you hold a Maryland Provisional License before advancing to a regular license?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Eighteen months of solo experience builds real-world judgment before passenger and curfew limits come off.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: What education, permit validity, and driving-record rules must be satisfied to earn a Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Letting your permit expire or picking up a PBJ blocks promotion even after finishing driver ed.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What signed paperwork and practical exam complete your upgrade from learner's permit to Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Handing over your signed sixty-hour or fourteen-hour log opens the gate to taking the behind-the-wheel test.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: What minimum birthday, Provisional time, and clean-record window unlock Maryland's final Driver's License?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Any moving conviction or PBJ resets the eighteen-month clean-record countdown toward full graduation.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: How does the MVA issue your upgrade from Provisional to full Driver's License, and what must you carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: No branch trip is needed, yet tossing your Provisional plastic away leaves your mailed attachment incomplete.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: What is the core supervision difference between driving on a learner's permit and driving on a Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Stepping into Provisional trades mandatory side-seat supervision for solo driving with temporary safety guardrails.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: What three eighteen-based benchmarks must all align before a Provisional holder earns a full license?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Remembering three eighteens locks in minimum age, Provisional tenure, and conviction-or-PBJ-free history together.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: When your full-license conversion card arrives in the mail, does it replace your Provisional card?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Officers expect to see both the mailed conversion card and your original Provisional photo license together.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: What three tests and special course must someone holding a license from another country complete in Maryland?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Foreign license holders bypass multi-month learner waits by completing vision, knowledge, skills, and three-hour safety ed.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: If an out-of-country license is not printed in English, what companion document or translation sources qualify?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Self-translated notes get rejected unless printed on approved provider, court translator, or embassy letterhead.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: Which three contact and verification details must appear on any translated license document?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Missing a phone number or signature invalidates an otherwise accurate foreign-language translation at the branch.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: When the knowledge test already exists in your language, how many attempts come before using an interpreter?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Applicants can only bring an interpreter for a supported language after trying the translated screen version five times.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Who covers interpreter costs at the MVA, and what credentials must that interpreter hold?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: While the MVA adds zero surcharge, your chosen interpreter must appear on the approved roster with valid photo ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: What kinds of testing accommodations can applicants with disabilities receive, and how are they tailored?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Matching tools like oral testing, screen readers, headphones, or sign language to individual needs keeps testing fair.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: What optional card can a driver with a developmental disability pick up at an MVA desk, and is proof required?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Carrying that optional wallet-sized blue card helps communicate clearly during traffic stops without filing medical records.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Combine Maryland's fee policy and supported-language attempt rule for using a test interpreter?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Remembering zero state fee, applicant-paid service, and five prior attempts covers every angle on interpreter rules.
sec02-card-sec02-R10.must_match_memory_hook: No MVA fee, self-paid, five tries

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What safety advantage do painted roadway lines give you compared with roadside posts?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Keeping your gaze right in your travel path preserves split-second reaction time when brake lights flare ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Why do highway crews paint certain stripes extra wide or add raised reflective markers?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Night rain turns flat asphalt into a dark mirror, so reflective studs and wide bars keep lane edges visible.
sec06-card-sec06-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Extra width and reflectors grab eyes

visual_sync.text_span: Extra width and reflectors grab eyes

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Compared with roads posted at forty-five or fifty miles per hour, how deadly are crashes at sixty-five or higher?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Crash energy climbs sharply with speed, overwhelming crumple zones that easily survive moderate suburban impacts.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Compared with roads posted at forty miles per hour or less, how likely is a crash at sixty-five or higher to be fatal?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing both federal highway safety multiples, so keep twice-as-deadly and nearly-five-times crystal clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What single habit does more than anything else to prevent death or severe injury in every seat on every trip?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Unbelted back-seat riders become heavy human projectiles during a rollover or head-on impact, hurting everyone inside.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Roughly what percentage of Maryland riders buckle up today, and what target has the state set?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: That remaining ten percent of unbuckled occupants accounts for a massive share of preventable highway fatalities statewide.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: About how many seconds does latching a seat belt take, and what could it prevent for most unbelted crash victims?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Skipping a three-second latch before shifting out of park trades effortless protection for life-altering ejection or trauma.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How do the two fatal-crash risk multiples compare as the gap widens below sixty-five miles per hour?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Pairing over-twice against forty-five to fifty with nearly-five-times against forty or under locks in a classic exam comparison.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What traffic flow does a single broken white line separate, and may you cross it to switch lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Always pair mirrors and a shoulder blind-spot check with your turn signal before crossing dashed white paint.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What directions of traffic does a single broken yellow center line divide, and what passing rule applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Because oncoming traffic shares that passing space, only pull out when sightlines are long and completely clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What two boundary or lane-separation jobs can a single solid white line perform?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Engineers paint solid white between turn bays, tunnels, or weave zones where sudden lane hops trigger side-swipes.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What rule applies where double solid white lines run side by side between same-direction lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Crossing twin solid white stripes cuts across protected express lanes, bridge approaches, or high-hazard merge barriers.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does lane-changing permission step down from broken white to single solid white to double solid white?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Test makers love asking whether single solid white bans lane shifts outright, when only double solid white truly prohibits them.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How do solid white and solid yellow edge lines help you tell your right road edge from your left edge?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Spotting solid yellow on your right side at night is an instant red alert that you entered a ramp or highway backward.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How does passing permission on a single broken yellow center line compare with double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Double yellow marks blind hills, curves, and busy stretches where crossing center invites an unavoidable head-on wreck.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: On divided highways, one-way streets, and ramps, which border of the roadway carries a single solid yellow line?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Keeping yellow to your left confirms you are traveling in the lawful flow direction on unfamiliar night ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What physical separation between opposing lanes makes a roadway an official divided highway?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Painted yellow lines alone never count as a physical divider when applying school-bus stopping laws on multi-lane roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Beyond banning routine lane shifts, what special lane type or roadway hazard can double solid white lines outline?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Buffer stripes stop abrupt diving into fast high-occupancy vehicle lanes and split traffic cleanly around fixed islands.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What special lane is framed by double broken yellow lines, and what controls when you may use it?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Because flow direction flips between morning and evening rush hours, entering without checking active lane beacons risks a head-on crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: How are the solid and broken yellow stripes arranged along each side of a two-way left-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Permit diagrams regularly flip inner and outer stripes to trick students who have not pictured solid-outside, dashed-inside geometry.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How can you tell a reversible lane apart from a two-way left-turn lane purely from yellow edge stripes?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Distinguishing twin dashed borders from solid-outer, broken-inner borders prevents cruising straight down a shared turn bay.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What traffic flow do double solid yellow lines separate, and who is allowed to pass across them?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Sight distance is restricted from both directions wherever twin solid yellow bars run down the center.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Even though passing is banned, when are you legally allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Students often confuse double solid yellow lines with raised concrete medians and miss that driveway left turns remain legal.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: On what kind of roadway do engineers paint one solid yellow stripe right beside one broken yellow stripe?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Crests and curves often open clear sightlines for drivers leaving a bend while blinding drivers entering it.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Along a mixed solid-and-broken yellow center line, which lane may pass carefully and which must hold back?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Pulling out across a solid stripe hugging your lane sends you blind into oncoming traffic hidden over a hill.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: What simple visual check tells you instantly whether passing is legal alongside a mixed yellow center pair?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Only the stripe touching your lane governs your sightline; the far stripe belongs strictly to oncoming drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How do double solid yellow lines treat overtaking a slow car compared with turning left into an entrance?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Overtaking keeps you head-on in opposing lanes far longer than waiting for a clean gap to turn into a driveway.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What three pieces of lane guidance or upcoming road changes can painted pavement words and symbols communicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Spotting merge arrows on asphalt early lets you blend smoothly before two lanes pinch down to one.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What do directional arrows and word messages painted inside a lane tell drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a turn-only arrow bay sideswipes adjacent drivers lawfully turning alongside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: What two sensitive zones lie ahead when giant school words or railroad crossing letters are painted on your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Oversized pavement stencils catch drivers whose view of roadside posts is blocked by buses, trees, or delivery vans.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What does a solid white bar painted across your lane show at a stop post or red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Stopping behind the white bar leaves turning radius clearance for large trucks and buses swinging onto your street.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: What row of painted shapes marks a yield line, and what must you do there?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Often nicknamed shark teeth at roundabouts and mid-block crossings, those triangles mark the exact spot to hold for walkers or cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: How are pedestrian crosswalks marked on the pavement, and how can their stripe pattern vary?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Whether painted as two parallel borders or high-visibility ladder bars, crosswalks belong to walkers and never serve as waiting zones.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How can you distinguish a stop line from yield lines by looking at the shapes painted across your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Confusing a solid white stop bar with painted yield triangles causes rolling-stop citations at intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Do most Maryland roadways where cyclists and drivers share space have special bike paint or posts?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Cyclists hold full legal road rights even on rural or neighborhood streets with zero bike symbols painted on asphalt.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Where do shared-use lane symbols mostly appear, and what three safety jobs do they serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Positioning cyclists away from parked car doors and wrong-way riding prevents urban dooring and intersection crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: How are bicycle-only lanes separated from motor vehicle travel lanes and identified on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Drifting or parking across solid or dashed bike-lane borders forces riders suddenly out into faster motor traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Where street parallel parking is allowed alongside a bike lane, how are those two spaces divided?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Check mirrors before swinging your car door open across that stripe so you never door an approaching cyclist.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: How does lane space under shared-use markings differ from a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Drivers share the exact same asphalt over sharrows, whereas white-bordered bike lanes stay reserved for two-wheeled traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way at street crossings, and must pedestrians obey traffic signals too?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Pedestrians hold priority in crossings, yet safe traffic flow requires people on foot to honor Walk and Don't Walk lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: At a crossing without traffic signals, when must you stop for a pedestrian—only on painted stripes or unmarked corners too?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Missing white paint never cancels pedestrian priority—drivers must stop fully for walkers in any legal crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which three groups of pedestrians need extra alertness and crossing time from drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Someone using a white cane, wheelchair, or walker may not hear horns or spot approaching cars and needs unhurried clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Do intersections without painted lines still have legal crosswalks where drivers must stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Sidewalk extensions across nearly every street corner form legal crosswalks even where zero paint touches the asphalt.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What is Maryland's strict rule when another vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: That stopped car or SUV is almost certainly shielding a pedestrian stepping right across your adjacent lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: During which two signal turns must you yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Both a green ball and a legal turn-on-red require letting pedestrians clear the crosswalk before your bumper crosses.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: When do police cars, fire engines, and ambulances hold the legal right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Active visual and audible warnings signal an urgent response where every second cleared on the road saves lives.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What three steps must you take the instant you see or hear a signaling emergency vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks fire trucks from turning—clear the box, hug the road edge, and wait until it passes.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Under what two rare exceptions may you pass an emergency vehicle running signals in your direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Overtaking a rolling ambulance or fire engine creates chaos unless the unit parks or an officer waves you past.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What does Maryland's Move-Over rule require when approaching a stopped emergency, tow, or service vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Shifting one full lane away—or dropping to a crawl ready to stop when boxed in—protects roadside responders from mirror strikes.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does your legal duty for a moving emergency vehicle differ from a stopped one on the shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Exam questions pair these two rules—pull to the edge and stop for rolling sirens, whereas roadside responders need an empty adjacent lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: How do large trucks handle intersection turns differently from passenger cars, especially before turning right?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Long trailers track tighter than cab wheels, forcing truckers to swing wide left so rear axles clear the right curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: When a truck ahead drifts left near an intersection, why should you hold back before passing on its right?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Mistaking a wide right-turn setup for a left lane change puts your car right into the closing trailer path.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What happens if you try to squeeze along the right side of a truck starting an intersection turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: As the cab pivots right, the long trailer sweeps inward across the right gap and pins cars against the sidewalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How should you pass a truck moving in your direction, and what mirror check clears you to merge back?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Lingering alongside a trailer keeps you invisible—move past cleanly and merge only once both rig headlights fill your rearview mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: How does creeping past a painted intersection stop line create a collision risk with large trucks?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Stop lines are set back specifically so eighteen-wheelers turning off the cross street have room to swing their trailers clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How does a loaded truck's weight compare with a typical car's, and how much stopping room can that rig need?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Cutting off a vehicle forty times heavier than a two-thousand-pound car leaves the trucker zero chance to stop in time.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How many major blind spots surround a large truck, and what term does the manual use for them?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Front, rear, left, and right no-zones swallow entire sedans completely out of the commercial driver's sight.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether you are sitting inside a truck or bus's side no-zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Light travels both ways in a mirror—if you cannot see the trucker's face in their side glass, you are hidden.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: How long and how wide is a large truck's right-side blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Because the driver sits high on the left cab side, the right-side blind wedge fans outward across three highway lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What two dangers make tailgating behind a truck or bus especially hazardous?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Box trailers block both the trucker's rear view and your forward sightline, trapping you if traffic halts ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: Compared with passenger cars, how much time and distance do trucks and buses need to stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Heavy commercial vehicles need almost twice the stopping cushion, so cutting into their front gap steals their emergency margin.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: After passing a truck or bus and seeing both headlights in your mirror, what must you avoid doing once in front?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Pulling in front of a heavy rig and immediately tapping the brakes forces forty tons of momentum straight toward your trunk.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Why must you never walk or drive behind a truck that is backing up?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Solid trailers leave a total rear blind zone without a center mirror, causing hundreds of backing deaths and injuries yearly.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: What quick visual rule keeps you out of a truck's side, rear, and front no-zones?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Spot the trucker's face beside it, hold well back behind it, and wait for both headlights before merging ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How many feet away must you stop when approaching a school bus with flashing red lights from behind or ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Holding twenty feet clear at both bumpers creates a protected safety corridor where children cross in front of the driver.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Which two cues allow you to start moving again after stopping for a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Late-running children often sprint toward the doors at the last second, so stay parked until red lights shut off or the bus rolls.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: When are oncoming drivers NOT required to stop for a school bus flashing red lights on a multi-lane road?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Only a raised median, concrete wall, or unpaved divider excuses opposite traffic—painted yellow stripes alone still require stopping.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: How do motorcyclists' road rights compare with car drivers', and how much higher is their crash injury risk?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Without steel doors, airbags, or seatbelts, motorcycle riders suffer injuries at six times the rate of passenger-car occupants.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Why must left-turning drivers look extra hard for oncoming motorcycles, and who is usually at fault in car-motorcycle crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Narrow motorcycle profiles make approaching speed look slower, leading car drivers to cause over half of two-vehicle bike crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What two-step visual check should you make before changing lanes or merging, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: A compact motorcycle disappears easily inside side-mirror blind spots unless you turn your head before moving laterally.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Why must you never squeeze beside a motorcycle in the same lane, even when the rider hugs one side?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Motorcyclists shift left and right across their lane deliberately to dodge potholes, handle crosswinds, and stay visible in mirrors.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Downshifting or rolling off a motorcycle throttle slows the bike rapidly without ever lighting up its rear brake lamp.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: How do you safely complete a pass around a motorcycle, and what should you do when a rider passes you?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Give wide side clearance until the bike's headlight shows in your rearview mirror, and keep steady speed when being overtaken.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: How should you handle signaling, merging, or speed around a group of motorcyclists?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Give early blinker notice, enter gaps between riders only when wide and safe, or ease back to let small groups clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: How does Maryland law classify bicycles on public roads, and what rules apply to riders?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Cyclists hold legal rights to use travel lanes while carrying the exact same duty to obey stop signs and signals.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: Which three traits make bicyclists vulnerable to severe injury or death from minor driver errors?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Slim bike frames blend into clutter quietly with zero crush protection when a distracted car drifts or clips them.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Where are bicycles prohibited in Maryland, and where else should you expect them anytime?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Outside interstates and tolled bridges or tunnels, expect cyclists day or night in every weather across streets and traffic circles.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Why is riding near the center of the travel lane often safest for a cyclist along narrow roads or parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Positioning mid-lane keeps riders clear of swinging car doors and roadside grates while deterring unsafe tight squeezes.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: When does Maryland law allow a slow-moving bicyclist to occupy the entire travel lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Whenever a lane lacks width for a car and bike to fit side by side with safe clearance, the cyclist owns it.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: What check must you perform every time before swinging open a parked car's door?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door into a bike lane gives an oncoming rider zero space to brake or swerve.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: What is Maryland's statewide default rule on sidewalk bicycling, whom must riders yield to, and who can restrict it?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Where town ordinances allow sidewalk riding, cyclists must always yield to walkers and wheelchair or mobility users.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when your motor vehicle turns or enters and crosses a bike lane or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Entering or cutting across a marked bike lane or shoulder requires yielding to through riders just like changing highway lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: What right-of-way do bicycles hold inside crosswalks, and what penalties hit if failing to yield causes a crash?
