sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Crosswalk cyclists hold full pedestrian priority, and causing a failure-to-yield collision brings heavy fines, prison exposure, and points.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: How should you adjust speed approaching a cyclist, and why should you keep off the horn?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast feet behind an open-air rider can startle them into wobbling straight into your path.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.question_text: How do bicyclists communicate turns, and why must you avoid following closely behind one?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.teaching_text: Broken glass or potholes harmless to car tires can flip a bike, forcing sudden swerves without brake-light warnings.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.question_text: What minimum clearance must you leave when passing any bicyclist, regardless of whether they ride in a bike lane or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.teaching_text: Wait until oncoming traffic clears so you can give a full three-foot cushion even when a painted stripe separates you.

sec09-card-sec09-F46.question_text: After overtaking a bicyclist, what visual check confirms you have enough space to move back right?
sec09-card-sec09-F46.teaching_text: Cutting back right too early clips the rider's front wheel—wait until the entire bike appears in your inside mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F48.question_text: Up to what speed can experienced cyclists travel, and what visual trap should drivers watch for?
sec09-card-sec09-F48.teaching_text: Assuming every bicycle crawls leads drivers to pull out or turn across fast road riders closing at city traffic pace.

sec09-card-sec09-F52.question_text: What move should you expect from a shoulder cyclist approaching a narrow bridge or row of parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F52.teaching_text: When the shoulder disappears at bridge railings or parked bumpers, the rider must blend left into main traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F53.question_text: What might a faint reflective glint ahead at night turn out to be, and which beams should you use near a cyclist?
sec09-card-sec09-F53.teaching_text: Small pedal or frame reflectors often mark a cyclist in the lane, and dropping to low beams avoids blinding the rider.

sec09-card-sec09-F54.question_text: Which age group of cyclists is most likely to turn abruptly without warning, and how do you protect them?
sec09-card-sec09-F54.teaching_text: Children lack traffic judgment and dart unpredictably, making strict residential and school-zone speeds lifesavers.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How do bicycle yield rules flip between intersection turns, crosswalks, and sidewalks?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Cars yield to cyclists on turns and crosswalks, whereas a cyclist riding along a sidewalk yields to pedestrians.
sec09-card-sec09-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Cars yield crossings, sidewalk bikes yield

visual_sync.text_span: Cars yield crossings, sidewalk bikes yield

sec09-card-sec09-F47.question_text: What path should you assume an unsignaling cyclist will take at an intersection, and how do you cross trails?
sec09-card-sec09-F47.teaching_text: Cyclists ride straight past right-turning cars unless signaling otherwise, and trail riders can approach briskly from either direction.
sec09-card-sec09-F47.must_match_memory_hook: Assume straight, scan trails both ways

visual_sync.text_span: Assume straight, scan trails both ways

sec09-card-sec09-F49.question_text: What dangerous turn must you never make right after overtaking a bicycle on a shoulder or bike lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F49.teaching_text: Overtaking a cyclist only to cut sharply right across their front tire causes classic right-hook intersection crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-F50.question_text: How should you check and position your car before making a right turn where bikes may ride?
sec09-card-sec09-F50.teaching_text: Scanning mirrors and your right blind spot before merging far right blocks bicycles from getting trapped inside your turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F51.question_text: Which two intersection moves around left turns put oncoming or curbside cyclists in immediate danger?
sec09-card-sec09-F51.teaching_text: Never cut left across an oncoming bike, and scan carefully before swinging right around a stopped left-turning car.

sec09-card-sec09-F55.question_text: Must moped and motor-scooter operators obey standard traffic laws, and why do drivers miss them?
sec09-card-sec09-F55.teaching_text: Narrow scooter silhouettes hide behind parked cars and A-pillars even though operators follow full roadway rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F56.question_text: Which roads may mopeds and scooters use in Maryland, and where in the roadway do they ride?
sec09-card-sec09-F56.teaching_text: Mopeds and scooters are legal on roads posted up to fifty miles per hour, riding single-file or two-abreast safely right.
sec09-card-sec09-F56.must_match_memory_hook: Posted fifty or less, keep right

visual_sync.text_span: Posted fifty or less, keep right

sec09-card-sec09-F57.question_text: What does ADAS stand for, and what share of crashes does the manual say proper use can prevent?
sec09-card-sec09-F57.teaching_text: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems cut collision odds substantially when paired with an attentive human behind the wheel.

sec09-card-sec09-F58.question_text: Which three safety features does the manual list as ADAS examples, and how do they detect hazards?
sec09-card-sec09-F58.teaching_text: Onboard cameras and radar sensors watch lane stripes, adjacent blind zones, and closing gaps to warn or assist.

sec09-card-sec09-F59.question_text: When driver-assistance tech is switched on, who remains legally and physically responsible for operating the vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F59.teaching_text: Assistance tech backs you up without replacing you—keep eyes scanning traffic, mirrors, and cameras continuously.

sec09-card-sec09-F60.question_text: Under which weather and road shapes can ADAS struggle, and why can't you assume two brands work alike?
sec09-card-sec09-F60.teaching_text: Rain, snow, fog, crests, and bends fool cameras, and marketing names vary widely across carmakers without matching actual limits.

sec09-card-sec09-F61.question_text: Which three maintenance and learning habits keep a vehicle's driver-assistance features working properly?
sec09-card-sec09-F61.teaching_text: Muddy camera lenses or skipped updates blind safety systems, and checking the manual or dealer clarifies exact alerts.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: How do alcohol and drugs affect your driving capability, and whom do impaired drivers put at risk?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Intoxicating substances strip away coordination and judgment so badly that safe driving turns impossible, threatening every walker and motorist nearby.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: What does BAC stand for, and what exact measurement does it describe?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Law enforcement uses Blood Alcohol Concentration to quantify how much alcohol is circulating in a driver's bloodstream.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Why can't you accurately estimate your BAC just by counting how many drinks you had?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Body weight, body fat percentage, and how much or how recently you ate all shift how fast alcohol enters your blood.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Beyond body size and food, which three personal factors change how strongly alcohol hits your driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Being tired, stressed, or on everyday pills magnifies alcohol's sedating and disorienting grip behind the wheel.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: In which three zones around your vehicle must you maintain constant awareness to drive safely?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Scanning mirrors and side lanes continuously prevents surprises when someone brakes ahead, tailgates behind, or drifts beside you.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: At what Blood Alcohol Concentration does Maryland classify a driver as under the influence of alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Hitting zero point zero eight triggers Maryland's per-se under-the-influence threshold regardless of how steady you think you feel.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Can you still face criminal charges in Maryland if your BAC tests below zero point zero eight?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Zero point zero eight is never a free pass—weakened judgment and coordination at lower readings still bring impaired-driving charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What three driving functions can suffer—and what happens to crash risk—after just a single drink?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Impairment starts with drink number one, dulling eyesight, basic muscle movements, and braking reflexes before you feel buzzed.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: How much alcohol may someone under age twenty-one legally consume in Maryland?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Maryland enforces an absolute zero-alcohol rule for anyone younger than twenty-one—not a lower casual allowance.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What license actions and extra charge hit an under-twenty-one driver stopped after drinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Underage licenses carry an explicit alcohol restriction, so drinking before driving risks both license loss and a restriction violation.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Where inside a motor vehicle is carrying an open alcohol container illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Even if the driver stays stone-sober, keeping unsealed liquor inside the cabin violates Maryland's open-container law.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What counts as an open container in Maryland, including when carrying a six-pack?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Many drivers get tripped up learning that a carton or ring missing cans—or holding empties—qualifies as an open container.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How does Maryland law define the passenger area for open-container rules?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Tucking an open bottle on the floorboard or in an unlocked console still counts because seated occupants can reach it.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do Maryland's zero point zero eight standard, lower-BAC impairment rule, and under-twenty-one rule fit together?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Keep all three layers clear—zero point zero eight is under-the-influence, lower readings still bring charges, and under-twenty-one allows zero.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Does putting an open bottle off the seat cushion make it legal inside the cabin?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Because passenger area spans everywhere a seated rider or driver can reach, only an inaccessible trunk keeps opened containers legal.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Which three categories of non-alcohol substances can severely damage alertness, focus, coordination, and reaction time?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Legal pharmacy prescriptions and household inhalants wreck mental focus and hand-eye timing just as badly as street drugs.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What three road cues become harder to judge or respond to under the influence of any drug?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Dulled perception leaves drugged drivers misjudging gaps while missing horns, sirens, and changing intersection lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What can happen to your Maryland license if you drive under the influence of controlled dangerous substances?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Controlled dangerous substances trigger severe administrative and court licensing losses even with zero alcohol in your system.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What warning should you check for on prescription and over-the-counter bottles, and what can ignoring it bring?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: A car counts as heavy machinery—driving impaired after ignoring a pharmacy warning sticker exposes you to criminal prosecution.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How can having a child in the vehicle change the sentence for a drunk or drugged driving conviction?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Endangering a young passenger lets a Maryland judge double both maximum incarceration and financial penalties on conviction.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which six unsafe behaviors define aggressive driving in the Maryland manual?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Stacking multiple reckless moves—speeding, bumper-riding, blowing signals, weaving, refusing to yield, and illegal passing—turns frustration into crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Which five everyday trip pressures commonly push ordinary motorists into aggressive driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Recognizing how congestion, construction bottlenecks, running late, and personal stress fuel impatience helps you defuse road rage early.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What three mindset and scheduling habits help you avoid aggressive-driving flare-ups?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Padding your departure schedule removes the urge to rush while minding your own driving keeps small slights from escalating.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Which four on-road courtesies keep traffic cooperative and defuse aggressive encounters?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Treating the highway like a race invites road rage—use blinkers, follow signs, give right-of-way, and let pushy drivers go.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What simple everyday principle does the manual give for sharing the road with others?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Giving merge gaps and forgiving honest mistakes builds the exact courtesy you hope for when navigating unfamiliar streets.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which three faculties does distracted driving pull away from the road—and which one matters above all?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Even with hands on the wheel and eyes forward, daydreaming or phone chatter steals the mental focus needed to react.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: Where does distracted driving rank among all causes of police-reported crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Inattention causes more police-investigated collisions than any other single factor because split-second glances miss stopped traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Beyond phones, what everyday cabin activities does the Maryland manual list as driving distractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Reaching for dropped items, tuning music, eating, applying makeup, or turning toward passengers blinds you just like texting.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What is Maryland's rule on holding a cell phone or texting while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: No motorist of any age may drive around Maryland holding a phone in hand for calls or messages.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: May a Maryland driver under age eighteen talk on a hands-free Bluetooth phone, and what is the sole exception?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Hands-free audio still splits young drivers' mental attention, so Maryland bans every non-emergency phone call under eighteen.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How do Maryland's cell-phone rules contrast between drivers eighteen and older versus drivers under eighteen?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Hand-held use is banned for everyone, while hands-free calling unlocks only once a driver turns eighteen.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Even though drivers eighteen and up may use hands-free devices, how often should they use the phone while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Legal hands-free conversations still tax your brain's reaction speed, so smart adult drivers keep calls rare.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What three safer habits should you use when a phone call needs to be made on a trip?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Handing phone duty to a passenger or parking safely off-road keeps zero cognitive load on the person steering.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What is the safest way to handle incoming phone calls and necessary conversations while driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Letting incoming rings roll straight to voicemail eliminates the scramble to answer mid-intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: Which three groups of motorists face an elevated risk of drowsy driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Long daily commutes, untreated sleep conditions, and sedating prescriptions quietly drain alertness well before bedtime.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: How does lack of sleep compare with alcohol or drugs in its effects on driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Missing sleep dulls reflexes, awareness, and decision-making much like intoxication, multiplying your odds of a highway crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Which four physical or mental symptoms warn that drowsiness is taking over at the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Blurry closing eyes, bobbing head posture, constant yawns, and disconnected thoughts mean microsleeps are seconds away.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Which four on-road mistakes reveal that you have grown dangerously drowsy?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Blanking on recent miles, blowing past exits, weaving across stripes, and fluctuating speed prove your focus has already dropped out.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: What is the best action to take the moment you feel tired or sleepy behind the wheel?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Cold air and loud music only mask exhaustion briefly—actual sleep or handing the wheel to a rested driver saves lives.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Why does trying to push through drowsiness fail, and what actually solves it?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Because exhaustion mimics alcohol impairment inside the brain, willpower cannot restore reaction speed—only rest or switching drivers works.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: What fraction of fatal crashes does the Maryland manual's campaign page attribute to distracted driving, and what leads the list?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Cell phones sit near the top of behaviors causing one out of every three deadly collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: Roughly what scale of impaired-driving arrests happen on Maryland roads every year?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Active impaired-driving enforcement across Maryland puts tens of thousands of drunk and drugged motorists in handcuffs annually.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: What two steps should you lock in before going out, and what financial and legal costs follow an impaired arrest?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Arranging a sober ride up front spares you jail exposure, steep fines, and thousands of dollars in court expenses.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Right after any collision, what two tools can you use to alert approaching traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Unwarned drivers cresting a hill or rounding a curve can slam straight into a fresh wreck.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What is your duty to remain on site if a crash hurts anyone, including a walker or cyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Driving off when a person on foot, on a bike, or in a car is injured turns an accident into a serious crime.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: When people are injured in a wreck, what must you report to nine one one and do with the cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Moving wrecked vehicles at an injury scene can worsen trauma and erase crucial crash evidence before responders arrive.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Which three urgent crash conditions involving injuries, vehicle condition, or driver sobriety always require calling police?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Test questions often hide an impaired driver or undrivable car inside a minor fender-bender scenario to check if you still dial police.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Beyond injuries or impairment, which three other crash situations involving licensing, fleeing, or damaged property require calling police?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Without an official police report, an unlicensed or fleeing motorist leaves you stuck paying for repairs or damaged public fixtures.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: During any roadside emergency, how should you handle the scene and why must your eyes stay on passing cars?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: A calm shoulder can turn deadly in a split second if a distracted driver drifts across the fog line.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does handling the vehicles after an injury crash compare with handling a drivable car when nobody is hurt?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars in live lanes after a minor tap invites a far worse secondary pileup.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What happens to your driver's license if you are convicted of fleeing a crash involving serious injury?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Test takers often guess a brief suspension, missing that Maryland revokes driving privileges outright for fleeing serious harm.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Up to how much prison time and fine money can fleeing a serious-injury crash bring?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Panic at the wheel can cost half a decade of freedom and thousands of dollars on top of losing your license.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: How does Maryland classify fleeing a fatal crash, and what are the maximum prison and fine penalties?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Walking or driving away when someone dies upgrades the charge to a felony with double the prison and fine ceilings.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: If no one is injured in a wreck but your car will not drive, whom do you call and what do you report?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Dispatchers prioritize ambulances first, so stating clearly that nobody is hurt lets officers route traffic control and towing fast.
sec10-card-sec10-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Call nine one one, report stuck

visual_sync.text_span: Call nine one one, report stuck

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: While waiting for help beside a vehicle that cannot be driven, what unsafe actions near the roadway must you avoid?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Stepping into live lanes to wave down strangers or dash across asphalt turns a stranded driver into a pedestrian casualty.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: When nobody is hurt and your car still drives after a collision, where should you position it and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Clearing the travel lane right away shields everyone from fast traffic and keeps minor fender-benders from gridlocking the road.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How do the top prison and fine numbers compare between leaving a serious-injury crash and leaving a fatal crash?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Pairing five years with five thousand and ten years with ten thousand makes this exam favorite effortless to recall.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Which seven pieces of personal, vehicle, and coverage information should every driver exchange after a crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Forgetting the plate state, license number, or insurer at the curb makes filing an accurate claim tough later on.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What three contact details should you request from bystanders who saw the collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Neutral bystanders leave quickly, and without ways to reach them their account cannot back you up if stories change.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Which four scene facts about where, when, vehicle count, and environment should you write down after a crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Adrenaline fades fast, so jotting down road and sky conditions on the spot stops guesswork weeks later.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How should you document the harm to the cars and the sequence of the collision before leaving?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Clear pictures paired with fresh written notes protect you against inflated repair bills or shifted blame.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Where must you pull over right after striking an unattended car or other unattended property?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Rolling blocks away looks like fleeing, while stopping squarely in a travel lane creates a fresh hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: After hitting unattended property, what should you try first, and what must you leave if the owner cannot be found?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Tucking a clear explanation with your contact details in an obvious spot fulfills your legal duty when nobody is around.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What does Maryland law require you to do immediately if your car strikes and hurts a dog, cat, horse, or cow?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Many drivers wrongly treat pets or livestock like roadside debris, not realizing failing to notify police right away breaks the law.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Why should you get a broken-down vehicle onto the shoulder whenever possible instead of stopping in a lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Roadside waits injure and kill motorists every year, so clearing live travel lanes is your primary survival move.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: Why is limping on a flat tire to an exit ramp or parking lot smart even if it ruins the wheel rim?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: A bent metal wheel is replaceable, whereas changing a tire inches from highway traffic puts your life on the line.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Which painted highway zone where an exit ramp branches off must you never use for stopping or parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Last-second exiters swerve across that striped wedge at highway speeds, leaving zero margin for a parked car.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: When remaining inside a broken-down vehicle is safe, how should you position yourself while waiting?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Unbuckling or twisting around in your seat defeats the airbags and crumple zones if a passing car clips your bumper.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: If staying inside a disabled car is too dangerous, how and where should everyone exit and shelter?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Lingering right beside a stalled car leaves you exposed if another vehicle plows into the breakdown.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: After evacuating a disabled vehicle, what terrain should you seek and which direction should you face?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Turning your back to approaching lanes blinds you to a drifting vehicle until it is too late to dodge.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Compare the right safety posture when you can stay inside a disabled vehicle versus when you must evacuate it?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Halfway choices like standing unshielded next to your door give you neither steel crash protection nor safe distance.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Why do officers issue citations, and what do you risk if you ignore an officer's instructions during a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Ignoring lawful commands during a roadside stop can turn a routine traffic ticket into handcuffs on the spot.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: According to Maryland's safety campaign, what three human factors cause many pedestrian and bicyclist injuries and deaths?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Crashes with walkers and riders rarely come from freak flukes, stemming instead from alcohol, forgotten rules, or distracted eyes.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: How often do motorcycle crashes injure the rider, and who causes over half of car-versus-motorcycle wrecks?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Without a steel cage around the rider, a car driver overlooking a bike in traffic usually leaves the motorcyclist injured.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: What specific habit does the Look Twice safety message urge drivers to practice before merging, switching lanes, or pulling out?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: A narrow motorcycle or bicycle hides easily behind a windshield pillar during a single rushed glance.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Where should you stop your car and which lights should you activate when police signal you over?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Giving the shoulder wide clearance and flipping on hazard lights protects both you and the approaching officer from passing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: Once stopped by an officer, which two things should you turn off and what should you do with your window?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: A quiet cabin and open window show you are staying put and make conversation clear from the start.
sec10-card-sec10-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Kill engine, mute radio, window down

visual_sync.text_span: Kill engine, mute radio, window down

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: What should you do with yourself and your seat belt while pulled over for a traffic stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Popping your door open looks threatening, and unbuckling before the officer arrives makes it seem like you drove unbelted.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: Where should your hands rest during a police stop, and what kind of cabin movements should you avoid?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Digging into a console or under a seat before being asked can look like hiding contraband or grabbing a weapon.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Why shouldn't you debate a traffic ticket on the shoulder, and where is the proper place to contest it?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Roadside arguments never erase a written citation and only prolong everyone's exposure to fast shoulder traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: Which vehicles on the roadway trigger Maryland's Move Over requirement when you approach from behind?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Exam traps try limiting the law to police cruisers, but Maryland covers any stopped, standing, or parked vehicle displaying flashing lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: When changing lanes for a flashing roadside vehicle is impossible or unsafe, what must you do and how do you judge it?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Forcing a blind lane change causes wrecks, so dropping speed to match weather, road, traffic, and people on foot is the lawful backup.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: What offense type, fine amount, and license point count come with a basic Move Over violation?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Even when nobody gets scratched, buzzing past flashing lights puts a criminal misdemeanor, fine, and point on your record.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: What fine and point penalty apply when failing to move over or slow down causes a collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Causing sheet-metal damage by crowding a roadside vehicle triples the license points and bumps the fine.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What fine and license points result when a Move Over violation involves serious injury or death?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Striking a roadside worker, trooper, or stranded motorist carries the steepest Move Over fine alongside three points.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: How does the MVA use license points, and what can accumulating them ultimately cost you?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Treating traffic tickets as pay-and-forget bills backfires once stacked MVA points suspend or revoke your privilege to drive.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Walk through all three Move Over fine and point tiers from a basic violation to a crash to serious harm or death?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Knowing that points jump from one to three as soon as a crash happens keeps every tier straight on test day.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: At which three licensing moments must you notify the MVA if you have a listed medical condition?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Waiting years until renewal after a mid-cycle diagnosis leaves you out of compliance with MVA health disclosure rules.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which MVA unit or board must clear your license if a listed medical condition could impact your driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Medical specialists review whether treatment keeps you safe on the road rather than leaving the call to counter staff.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: What specific blood-sugar event and timeframe make diabetes reportable to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Well-managed diabetes alone is not the trigger; needing another person's help for low sugar recently flags crash risk.
sec12-card-sec12-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Assisted low sugar within six months

visual_sync.text_span: Assisted low sugar within six months

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: When must a driver report a heart condition to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Passing out from a cardiac issue means a repeat episode behind the wheel could leave a moving car uncontrolled.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Falling short of what corrected visual acuity in one eye or what binocular field angle makes an eye issue reportable?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Sharp straight-ahead reading plus wide side vision work together so you catch both signs ahead and cross-traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Which five neurological, blackout, sleep, or brain-injury conditions appear on the MVA's reportable list?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Any condition capable of causing sudden unconsciousness or microsleep at highway speed requires MVA medical review.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: When must arm, hand, leg, or foot weakness, shaking, numbness, or an impaired or missing limb be reported?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Adaptive hand controls or pedal aids often solve physical limits once the MVA evaluates how they affect steering and braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Which substance-use, mental health, and cognitive conditions must also be disclosed to the MVA?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Safe driving relies on steady judgment and memory just as heavily as eyesight and physical reflexes.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: Which vehicles may a Maryland Learner's Permit holder operate, and who must always ride along?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Holding a passenger-car permit never authorizes hopping onto a motorcycle or driving solo down the block.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What is the minimum age required to serve as a supervising driver for a permit holder?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: An eighteen-year-old sibling with a full license is still too young to legally supervise your practice drives.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How many years of licensing must a supervising driver hold, and do out-of-state licenses or vehicle class matter?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Maryland counts valid years from another state, provided that license covers the exact vehicle class you are practicing in.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Where inside the vehicle must your supervising driver sit, and which vehicle is the sole exception?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: A supervisor relaxing in the back row cannot coach effectively or reach the wheel in a split-second emergency.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Starting at what age may someone register as an organ donor on their own?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Turning eighteen lets you decide independently without needing a parent or guardian's signature.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: At what age may a minor register as an organ donor, and whose permission is required?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds can enroll at permit or license time as long as a parent or guardian signs off in writing.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What can appear on your Maryland license if you opt into organ donation while applying or renewing?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Printing that designation directly on your card lets hospital teams honor your wish immediately when seconds count.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: Under the nineteen ninety-three federal Motor Voter law, what voting service must the MVA offer eligible license or ID applicants?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Bundling voter registration with license transactions saves eligible citizens a separate trip before election deadlines.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: What licensing requirement applies to the insurance company covering any Maryland-registered vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Buying coverage from an insurer not licensed in Maryland leaves a registered vehicle out of compliance with state law.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: Which two kinds of liability coverage must Maryland vehicle owners carry, and where are the required minimums posted?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Liability coverage pays for people hurt and property damaged in crashes you cause up to state-mandated minimums listed online.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: In what formats may you carry your valid insurance ID card while driving, and what happens if you cannot show an officer?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Pulling up a current electronic card on your phone during a traffic stop counts just like carrying a paper slip.
sec12-card-sec12-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Paper or digital proof avoids fines

visual_sync.text_span: Paper or digital proof avoids fines

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Who inside a motor vehicle must wear a seat belt or be strapped into a child safety seat under Maryland law?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Unbelted back-seat riders become dangerous human projectiles in a crash, so Maryland covers every seat in the car.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: How do airbags protect best alongside your belts, and how many inches should separate your chest from the steering wheel?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Sitting right on top of the wheel puts your chest inside the airbag's explosive inflation zone instead of its cushion.
sec12-card-sec12-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Buckled, ten to twelve inches back

visual_sync.text_span: Buckled, ten to twelve inches back

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: How should a pregnant person position both the lap belt and the shoulder strap while riding or driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Routing the lap strap across the hip bones and thighs rather than over the abdomen shields both parent and baby in a sudden stop.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Compare the minimum age for a learner's supervising driver against the ages for independent and parental-consent organ donation?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Exam writers love mixing age milestones across chapters, so keeping twenty-one, eighteen, and sixteen distinct pays off fast.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Under what age must a child use a child safety seat, and what height lets a younger child transition out?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Standard vehicle belts ride across a small child's neck and belly until they reach four feet nine inches.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Until what age or seat limit must a young child ride rear-facing in a federally compliant car seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle a toddler's heavy head and fragile spine during frontal impacts far better than forward straps.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: Whose two sets of instructions govern child seat setup, and what devices count as child safety seats?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Even an approved car seat or booster fails in a crash if anchored in a spot your car's manual forbids.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Which Maryland Department of Health program offers low-cost car and booster seat rentals when families cannot afford one?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Knowing this state rental resource exists helps families buckle kids legally, though local availability varies.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Where must you never install a rear-facing infant or toddler car seat?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: An inflating passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing shell right where the baby's head rests.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Where should kids younger than thirteen ride, and how should they be restrained?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Front seats are engineered around adult frames, making the back row far safer until a rider reaches thirteen.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What do anti-lock braking systems prevent during hard braking, and why does that matter?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Locked tires slide straight ahead no matter how you turn the wheel, whereas rolling tires let you steer around trouble.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: How does ABS react when a wheel starts locking, and what sound and pedal feel might surprise a driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: New drivers who get startled by the rumble and pulsing pedal often lift their foot right when they should stay firm.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: What is Maryland's rule on driving with earplugs, headsets, or earphones, and what device is permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Sealing off both ears drowns out sirens, horns, and train bells, while medical hearing aids enhance road sounds instead.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: Up to how much in annual fines per vehicle can failing to carry required auto insurance bring in Maryland?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Letting coverage lapse quickly costs far more in state penalties than keeping an active policy in force.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Line up the three age cutoffs for rear-facing seats, child safety seats, and riding in the back row?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Remembering the height escape hatch of four feet nine inches alongside ages two, eight, and thirteen nails every child-restraint question.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Where does parallel parking still show up in Maryland training, even though it was dropped from the road test?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: City curbs still demand parallel parking in real life, which is why driver education keeps teaching it.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Which driving-course maneuver evaluates the exact same vision, space, mirror, signal, and pedal skills as parallel parking?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Examiners can grade every low-speed observation and car-control habit inside one tight backing turn.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Which three parking and turnaround maneuvers must you perform during the Maryland driving test?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Practicing both nose-in and reverse stall entries plus tight turnarounds prepares you for the exact closed-course checklist.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: What are the exact foot dimensions of the test parking stall and the three-point turn box?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Setting cones to ten by twenty and sixteen by twenty feet in an empty lot lets you rehearse the exact test geometry.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Summarize which classic parking move is off the Maryland driving test versus which three maneuvers are required?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Focusing practice hours on pull-in, back-in, and three-point turns matches what the examiner actually scores.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: How should bicyclists position themselves in a group, handle hazards and car doors, treat walkers, and follow traffic controls?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Riding predictably in a straight line outside the door zone helps drivers anticipate your path and prevents sudden swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: On which side of the road must bicyclists travel, and how should they position themselves at intersections?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Pedaling against oncoming cars surprises turning drivers, whereas matching traffic flow and intersection lanes keeps movements readable.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: What two checks and signals should a bicyclist complete before shifting lanes or turning?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Bikes lack side mirrors and brake lights, making a shoulder glance and clear hand signal vital before moving laterally.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: What are the two safe ways a bicyclist can complete a left turn at an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Busy multi-lane junctions let riders choose between merging into the left turn lane or walking the crosswalk on foot.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: How do rain or snow change bicycle braking, and which two road surfaces get especially slick?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Narrow bike tires lose grip fast on wet lane stripes and metal utility lids while wet rims take longer to bite.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.question_text: How must a bicycle carry a young child or small packages so the rider stays in full control?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.teaching_text: Dangling bags off handlebars yanks steering off line, so racks or baskets keep both hands planted firmly on the bars.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: In the handbook's night-riding paragraph, what front light, rear reflector, and visibility distance does state law require?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Notice the handbook gives two slightly different distance citations on the same page, with this paragraph stating six hundred feet.
sec12-card-sec12-F42.must_match_memory_hook: White front, red rear, six hundred

visual_sync.text_span: White front, red rear, six hundred

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: In the bicycle equipment list, from how many feet must the white headlight and red rear reflector each be visible?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Spotting that the equipment bullet lists five hundred feet up front and six hundred behind prevents getting tripped up on specifics.
sec12-card-sec12-F43.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred front, six hundred rear

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred front, six hundred rear

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: Who is legally required to wear a bicycle helmet in Maryland, including non-steering riders?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Kids riding in bike seats or trailers face the same pavement impact as the person pedaling, so the under-sixteen law covers passengers too.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.question_text: Within how many feet must legal bicycle brakes bring a bike to a stop from ten miles per hour on clean, dry, flat pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.teaching_text: Worn brake pads that stretch a ten-mile-per-hour stop past fifteen feet leave a cyclist unable to halt before a sudden pull-out.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.question_text: What pedal, wheel-count, and maximum motor-wattage rules define an electric bicycle in Maryland?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.teaching_text: Once a motor exceeds seven hundred fifty watts or drops working pedals, the machine no longer qualifies as an e-bike.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.question_text: When does a Class one electric bicycle provide motor help, and at what speed does that assist cut off?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.teaching_text: Because the motor helps only while your feet turn the cranks and stops at twenty, Class one rides closest to a standard bike.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.question_text: How does a Class two electric bicycle deliver motor assistance, and at what speed does it stop helping?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.teaching_text: Class two shares the same twenty-mile-per-hour ceiling as Class one, but its throttle can propel the bike while coasting.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.question_text: How is motor help triggered on a Class three electric bicycle, and what is its cutoff speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.teaching_text: Drivers misjudge approaching Class three bikes easily because pedal assist carries riders close to city traffic speeds.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.question_text: What rider limit, weight cap, frame setup, and top powered speed define an electric low-speed vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.teaching_text: Doubling up a friend on a standing scooter violates its single-operator design and destabilizes the small deck.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.question_text: Which two wheel layouts qualify as an electric low-speed vehicle, and what should riders verify locally?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.teaching_text: Cities and towns can restrict where stand-up electric scooters roll even when the machine meets state hardware specs.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Contrast Class one, Class two, and Class three electric bicycles by pedaling requirement and cutoff speed?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Grouping the two twenty-mile-per-hour classes first and spotting Class two as the non-pedaling outlier makes all three stick.
sec12-card-sec12-R01.must_match_memory_hook: One-three pedal, two coasts, three fastest

visual_sync.text_span: One-three pedal, two coasts, three fastest

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What credential do you need before operating any car, van, or pickup truck on Maryland roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Cars, vans, and pickups all count legally as motor vehicles, so driving even a short block unlicensed breaks Maryland law.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What does Maryland's vision screening measure, and which two providers are allowed to perform it?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Getting screened ahead of time at your own optometrist or ophthalmologist can streamline your branch appointment.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Where should a Maryland applicant look for next steps after falling short of the standard vision numbers?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Falling short on the first chart check is not always the end because online MVA guidance explains follow-up review paths.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which section of the Maryland manual explains how to set up special accommodations for the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Arranging support tools before arriving at the branch ensures extra time, audio, or sign-language help is ready.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What online practice tool does the MVA provide, and what else must you study alongside it?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Sample tutorial questions build familiarity, yet skipping chapters of the manual leaves big blind spots on test day.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What does Maryland's driving skills test verify, and which two driving environments does it combine?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Practicing only parking-lot cones or only neighborhood streets leaves you half-prepared when the examiner grades both.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Can you walk in unscheduled for the Maryland driving skills test, or how must you set it up?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Examiner slots require advance scheduling, so showing up without a confirmed web or phone booking wastes the trip.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What three health and wellness guidelines does the MVA share for skills-test day inside the car?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Cracking windows helps cabin airflow, masks remain welcome, and rescheduling when sick protects both you and the examiner.
sec01-card-sec01-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Fresh air, optional mask, reschedule sick

visual_sync.text_span: Fresh air, optional mask, reschedule sick

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What top fine or jail time can highway littering bring in Maryland, and how much trash do crews clear yearly?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Tossing trash out a window risks steep criminal penalties and adds to millions of pounds crews haul off roads.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: Compare where you may complete Maryland's vision screening versus where you must take the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Outside eye doctors can certify your vision form, whereas written knowledge testing stays strictly inside MVA branches.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which three screenings or tests must you pass to meet Maryland's core licensing requirements?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Every new driver proves clear eyesight, solid rulebook recall, and calm behind-the-wheel control before earning full privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How does a Maryland applicant find out whether additional safety requirements apply to their license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Individual driving or medical histories sometimes require extra clearance steps that branch staff flag directly for you.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which three subject areas are evaluated on Maryland's driver knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Studying only sign shapes without statutory rules and defensive habits leaves two-thirds of the question bank uncovered.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Where do every single one of Maryland's knowledge-test questions come from, and where do you sit for it?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Zero trick topics come from outside sources because every question maps back to the official Maryland manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What health disclosure does Maryland law require from drivers, and which manual section covers the details?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Conditions that trigger blackouts, seizures, or impaired control must be self-reported promptly under Section ten rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does what the knowledge test measures differ from what the driving skills test evaluates?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Knowing laws, habits, and signs comes first on screen before proving physical control on roads and lot courses.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does reporting a driving-related medical condition differ from MVA extra safety requirements in who speaks up first?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Waiting for the state to guess a health condition violates your personal legal duty to disclose it.
sec01-card-sec01-R08.must_match_memory_hook: You report medical; MVA flags extras

visual_sync.text_span: You report medical; MVA flags extras

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What does Maryland's binocular vision standard require your eyes to do?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Coordinated two-eye sight gives depth perception needed to judge closing gaps when merging or turning.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What minimum visual acuity score must you reach in each eye for a standard Maryland license?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Clear distance sharpness lets you read highway exit panels and warning legends well ahead of braking zones.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: At least how many degrees wide must your continuous field of vision be to qualify in Maryland?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Wide peripheral sight spots cyclists, kids, and cross-street cars approaching from the corners of your eyes.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What two rules apply if you rely on glasses or contact lenses to pass Maryland's vision screening?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Driving without required corrective lenses counts as violating a license restriction if pulled over.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does Maryland's twenty-over-forty standard differ in what it measures from the one-hundred-forty-degree standard?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Passing letter-chart clarity in each eye alone is not enough without wide continuous side-to-side awareness.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Name all three vision standards a standard Maryland license applicant must satisfy together?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Locking all three eyesight benchmarks together ensures every question on Maryland's vision screening is an instant point.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Does needing prescription glasses or contacts block you from getting a Maryland license, and how is it handled?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Corrected twenty-over-forty vision qualifies cleanly so long as your lenses stay on whenever you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Who supplies the car for Maryland's driving skills test, and what tag paperwork must it carry?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Examiners inspect tags and registration cards curbside before ever climbing into the passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: What financial protection must you prove for the vehicle brought to your Maryland skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Showing up without verifiable insurance proof cancels your road test before the wheels turn an inch.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What mechanical and windshield standards must your skills-test car pass before going out?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Spiderweb glass cracks or dangling mirror charms block sightlines and trigger an automatic equipment turn-away.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: How much fuel must be in the tank of the vehicle you bring to the Maryland skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Running low mid-exam risks stalling on public roads, so examiners verify at least half a tank upfront.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Who must come with a learner to the skills-test site, and where are their qualifications listed?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Permit holders cannot drive solo to the MVA lot, making a qualified Section ten mentor mandatory.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Who is allowed inside the cabin during the driving skills test, including the sole exception?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Keeping parents, friends, and pets out of the back seat eliminates coaching and distractions during grading.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does your supervising driver's role change once the examiner begins your behind-the-wheel test?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Your mentor legally escorts you onto the lot, then waits outside while you, the examiner, and any interpreter ride.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Separate the skills-test vehicle checklist into its paperwork items versus its physical car conditions?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Checking registration and insurance in your folder plus glass, safety, and half-tank fuel avoids turn-aways.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: What does visibility mean behind the wheel, and which four conditions most commonly cut it down?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Losing clear sight of walkers, cars, signs, and lane stripes shrinks your reaction window whenever weather or nightfall rolls in.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: When fog, darkness, or storms make it hard to see ahead, what part of the roadway should guide your steering?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Tracking the right pavement edge keeps your car centered in its lane without staring straight into blinding oncoming glare.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Which side of your vehicle must yellow pavement markings stay on, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Spotting yellow paint on your right means you have drifted into opposing lanes or onto a wrong-way ramp.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Which two roadway boundaries or lane divisions do white pavement markings indicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: White stripes confirm traffic beside you moves in your direction while marking the outer right boundary of the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What two safety jobs do your headlights perform when visibility drops?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Even when twilight still lets you spot the pavement, unlit cars blend into gray backgrounds for oncoming drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Which three everyday conditions does the Maryland manual highlight as prime times to switch on your headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Flipping headlights on manually in storms and fog ensures both front lamps and rear taillights mark your position.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What is traction, which three maneuvers depend on it, and how do wet roads change it?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Water between rubber and asphalt slashes friction, stretching braking distances and making every turn easier to slide out.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Why must you drop speed in bad weather, and what tire upkeep standard should you maintain?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Easing off the gas buys extra seconds to react while healthy tread grooves channel slush and rainwater away.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Which abrupt steering and pedal habits must you avoid when driving in bad weather?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Sudden steering yanks or sharp throttle and brake changes snap fragile wet-road grip and start an instant skid.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Before heading into bad weather, what equipment should you check and what lights should you run?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Streaking wiper blades blind you in heavy spray, and running headlights makes your car stand out through rain curtains.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Which two vehicle reservoirs should you keep topped up throughout winter?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Extra gas keeps the heater running if traffic stalls in snow, while washer fluid clears salty highway spray.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: Which seven survival and traction supplies belong in your car's emergency kit?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Packing warning flares, warmth, batteries, a small shovel, an ice scraper, and kitty litter or sand turns strandings manageable.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Which five road-surface hazards—plus what driver choice—cut tire traction and invite skids?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Sand, gravel, rough patches, oil slicks, and puddles all weaken tire bite, especially when combined with excess speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: At what forward visibility distance does Maryland require you to switch on your headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Do not wait for pitch-black skies—anytime haze, dusk, or rain blocks clear sight a thousand feet out, flip lights on.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What does Maryland law require whenever inclement weather has your windshield wipers running?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Daytime automatic light sensors often miss bright rainstorms, so flip full headlights on manually whenever wipers sweep.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: In which everyday night setting and three weather conditions should you run low-beam headlights?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Low beams angle downward onto the lane instead of reflecting blinding glare off precipitation droplets or city traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Why does Maryland advise turning on low beams when entering tunnels or construction zones even if not always mandated?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Sudden shade inside tunnels and dusty cone lanes hide unlit vehicles from road crews and surrounding traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: What kind of roadways are high-beam headlights designed for, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Where streetlights disappear, high beams project light much farther down-lane to reveal dark pedestrians and vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: At least how many feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim high beams to low?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Leaving brights on inside five hundred feet blinds the approaching driver right as your two cars close rapidly.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Within what distance behind a vehicle you are following must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: High beams inside three hundred feet bounce off the lead driver's mirrors and blind them from behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Which two visual limitations make driving at night riskier than daytime driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Darkness strips away peripheral landmarks for judging closing speed while capping forward sight to your headlight reach.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes—and where must you avoid staring—when bright oncoming headlights approach at night?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Staring straight into bright bulbs leaves temporary night blindness after the car passes, whereas tracking the right edge preserves vision.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: How should you adjust your following gap at night, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Because darkness delays spotting unlit hazards or sudden brake lights ahead, extra space prevents rear-end crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How does Maryland's oncoming dimming distance compare with its following dimming distance?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Exam choices swap these two numbers constantly—remember oncoming headlights hit eyes directly, needing the longer five-hundred-foot dim.
sec07-card-sec07-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How should you adjust your speed in fog, especially once headlights or taillights appear ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Lights glowing in fog could belong to a crept-to-a-halt vehicle or someone drifting across the centerline.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: What two steps should you take when fog grows too dense to keep driving safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Stopping partway in a travel lane invites a rear-end hit—clear the pavement completely and flash hazard lights.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Which headlight setting—and optional lamps—should you use in fog?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: High beams reflect off airborne mist straight back into your windshield, whereas low beams and fog lamps cut underneath.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: How does the safe following gap change as pavement goes from dry to wet to snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Every drop in surface friction stretches stopping distance further, demanding a much bigger gap on rain and bigger still on ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Why must you avoid slamming the brakes, and how do you prevent skidding in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Locking non-ABS wheels turns your tires into unsteerable sled runners, whereas controlled pumping keeps them rolling.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Which roadway structures freeze before regular streets, and why can plowed roads still turn icy?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Elevated decks chill from underneath first, while daytime snowmelt on plowed asphalt refreezes into slick patches overnight.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What is black ice, and how does it form on asphalt?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Because the thin refrozen sheet lets dark pavement show right through, drivers mistake deadly glare ice for harmless wet road.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Is there any guaranteed safe speed on snow and ice, and why do winter conditions shift from block to block?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Sunlight, tree shade, and uneven salt spreading can turn grip into sheer ice around a single corner.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Does driving a four-wheel-drive vehicle make you immune to sliding on snow and ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Powering all four wheels helps you pull away from stops without adding extra tire friction for braking or cornering on ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What must you brush and scrape completely clear before driving in snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Driving with crusted lamps or frosted side glass hides your turn signals and blinds you to cross traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Which three gentle habits should you use when starting, checking grip, and approaching turns on snow or ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Feathering away from stops, feeling brake bite gently, and slowing well ahead of corners keeps tires from breaking loose.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: When Maryland declares a snow emergency, which three tire or traction options qualify on designated snow emergency routes?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Unprepared cars spinning out block plows and ambulances, so designated routes mandate proper winter rubber or chains.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: The instant your vehicle starts skidding, what is your very first move with the pedals?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Whether heavy gas or hard braking triggered the slide, releasing pedal force lets overloaded tires start rolling straight again.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: Which direction do you steer and where do you look while recovering from a skid?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Focusing your eyes down the intended lane guides smooth steering corrections instead of staring straight into a guardrail.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: During a skid, when is it safe to touch the brake again, and what can help if rear wheels lose grip?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Braking mid-slide locks skidding tires worse, whereas waiting for bite—or feathering light throttle on rear slip—stabilizes the chassis.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: What physically happens between your tires and the pavement when your car hydroplanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Excess speed over deep water lifts rubber off the asphalt completely, robbing you of steering and braking control.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: What two simple steps prevent hydroplaning before it starts?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Good tread depth evacuates water beneath the tire footprint while lower speeds give water time to clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: What four-part response brings your car safely down if it starts hydroplaning?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Holding the wheel straight with zero braking lets your speed bleed off naturally until the tires touch asphalt again.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does the braking rule during hydroplaning differ from braking during a road skid?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Keep these two water-and-ice questions clear—hydroplaning forbids braking completely, while skid recovery allows braking once tires bite.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: What basic fact about trains makes extra caution essential at every railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: A freight or passenger train takes a massive distance to halt, meaning the car driver is the only one able to yield.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.question_text: Which three types of vehicles must stop before every railroad crossing, even when no warning lights flash?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.teaching_text: Leave extra following space behind transit buses, yellow buses, and placarded tankers near tracks so their required stop never surprises you.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.question_text: What must you assume about train schedules, directions, and how close or fast a locomotive appears?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.teaching_text: A locomotive's large size creates an optical illusion that makes its closing speed look deceptively slow until it is too late.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.question_text: What do flashing crossing lights or lowered gates mean, and when may you proceed?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.teaching_text: Driving around lowered arms or starting while red lights still flash risks getting struck on a neighboring track.
sec07-card-sec07-F45.must_match_memory_hook: Stop until gates rise, lights off

visual_sync.text_span: Stop until gates rise, lights off

sec07-card-sec07-F46.question_text: Once the last railcar clears a crossing, why must you look both ways before moving?
sec07-card-sec07-F46.teaching_text: On multi-track crossings, the caboose or final car of one train can screen a fast locomotive approaching from the opposite way.

sec07-card-sec07-F47.question_text: What two clearance checks must be true before your front bumper enters railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F47.teaching_text: Rolling onto tracks behind backed-up traffic can trap your car across the rails with nowhere to pull forward.

sec07-card-sec07-F48.question_text: If an emergency strands your vehicle on or near railroad tracks, what do you do first and how do you report it?
sec07-card-sec07-F48.teaching_text: Evacuate everyone well away from the rails first, then call the railroad number posted at the crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F59.question_text: What defines a limited-access highway, and what makes an interstate a specific kind of one?
sec07-card-sec07-F59.teaching_text: Replacing cross-traffic intersections and signals with controlled ramps keeps high-speed freeway traffic flowing smoothly across state lines.

sec07-card-sec07-F49.question_text: What activities create a work zone, and does a work zone always stay parked in one spot?
sec07-card-sec07-F49.teaching_text: Line-painting, pothole patching, and mowing convoys roll slowly down active lanes just like fixed construction sites.

sec07-card-sec07-F50.question_text: Which five roadway changes should you anticipate inside a work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F50.teaching_text: Missing shoulders, uneven asphalt edges, and sudden lane shifts leave zero room for drifting or following closely.

sec07-card-sec07-F51.question_text: Which background color marks work-zone signage, and what mindset should it trigger?
sec07-card-sec07-F51.teaching_text: Spotting diamond orange warnings ahead is your cue to lift off the throttle and scan for cones or flaggers.

sec07-card-sec07-F52.question_text: What do flashing amber or yellow lights inside a Maryland work zone tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F52.teaching_text: Human road crews are standing just feet from live traffic whenever yellow beacons flash, so slow down and obey instructions.

sec07-card-sec07-F53.question_text: What do flashing blue lights in a Maryland work zone indicate, and how do speeding fines behave there?
sec07-card-sec07-F53.teaching_text: Automated work-zone speed cameras issue steep tickets—and penalties climb higher still when crew members are on site.

sec07-card-sec07-F54.question_text: Which vehicles in or ahead of Maryland work zones may display flashing green lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F54.teaching_text: Recognizing green strobes helps you spot slow service trucks and snow or maintenance gear well before the cones start.

sec07-card-sec07-F55.question_text: Which six driving habits keep everyone safe while passing through an active work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F55.teaching_text: Putting away distractions, merging smoothly, holding your lane, leaving space, and obeying flaggers prevents chain-reaction work-zone crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How do flashing amber, flashing blue, and flashing green lights differ inside Maryland work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Maryland's permit exam loves testing these three beacon colors side by side—lock in workers, cameras, and maintenance trucks.
sec07-card-sec07-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Amber workers, blue cameras, green crews

visual_sync.text_span: Amber workers, blue cameras, green crews

sec07-card-sec07-F56.question_text: What traffic control greets roads entering a traffic circle, and who always holds the right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F56.teaching_text: Vehicles already circulating have priority so the circle never gridlocks—wait for a safe opening before entering.

sec07-card-sec07-F57.question_text: How do you approach a roundabout regarding speed, the center island, crosswalks, and an empty circle?
sec07-card-sec07-F57.teaching_text: Stay right of the center island, yield to crosswalk walkers, wait at the line for traffic—or roll smoothly in if clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F58.question_text: In a multi-lane traffic circle, how should you hold lanes and set up your exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F58.teaching_text: Hold your lane around the curve, then signal right after passing the exit before yours to move smoothly outside.

sec07-card-sec07-F60.question_text: How should you use an entrance ramp and acceleration lane, and what painted boundary must you not cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F60.teaching_text: Build up to freeway pace inside the acceleration lane and wait until solid gore lines end before merging.

sec07-card-sec07-F61.question_text: Which lane must you use whenever possible if you are traveling slower than surrounding highway traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F61.teaching_text: Camping in left lanes below traffic pace forces dangerous right-side passing and stacks impatient cars behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F62.question_text: When leaving a highway, when do you move right, where do you start braking, and what speed do you hit?
sec07-card-sec07-F62.teaching_text: Braking hard inside fast through-lanes invites rear-end collisions—wait until your tires enter the deceleration lane to slow.

sec07-card-sec07-F63.question_text: What must you do—and never do—if you accidentally take the wrong highway exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F63.teaching_text: Backing up on a ramp or freeway shoulder puts you head-on against sixty-mile-per-hour exiting traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F64.question_text: When is stopping on a highway shoulder permitted, and what two safety steps apply once parked there?
sec07-card-sec07-F64.teaching_text: High-speed shoulders are breakdown zones only—switch hazard lights on and remain buckled inside rather than standing near traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F65.question_text: Which two light settings must vehicles in a Maryland funeral procession run, and what privilege does that grant at red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F65.teaching_text: Keeping headlights and four-way flashers active identifies the convoy so all cars stay together safely through red signals.

sec07-card-sec07-F66.question_text: If your traffic light turns green while a lit funeral procession is crossing, what must you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F66.teaching_text: Never cut between lit procession cars on a green light unless your turn path never crosses their line.

sec07-card-sec07-F67.question_text: Which road users qualify as slow-moving vehicles, and what top speed does the rear emblem warn of?
sec07-card-sec07-F67.teaching_text: Farm tractors, buggies, and bikes close toward your windshield shockingly fast when highway cars approach a twenty-five-mph vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F68.question_text: How should you drive behind a slow-moving vehicle, and what signal warns drivers approaching behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F68.teaching_text: Switching on your four-way flashers alerts fast-approaching drivers behind you that traffic has slowed dramatically ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: What is the exact functional difference between an acceleration lane and a deceleration lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: One builds speed to blend seamlessly into freeway traffic while the other sheds speed safely off the main lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: How does Maryland view driving legally, and why might the MVA attach restrictions to your license?
